result.title: Default clone link-mode on macOS causes ~17s syspolicyd rescan on every venv recreate
result.body:
### Summary

On macOS, the default `--link-mode clone` creates new inodes for every `.so` file on each `uv pip install`. macOS syspolicyd (Gatekeeper) caches its security scan results per-inode, so every venv recreate triggers a full rescan of all native extensions — adding ~17s of wall time for a typical data science stack (pandas, polars, pyarrow, jupyterlab).

`--link-mode hardlink` avoids this because hardlinks share the uv cache's inodes, and syspolicyd recognizes them as already scanned.
## Reproduction

```bash
# Install a typical data-science stack
uv venv && VIRTUAL_ENV=.venv uv pip install pandas polars pyarrow jupyterlab

# First import — slow (~18s), expected
time .venv/bin/python -c "import pandas, polars, pyarrow"

# Second import — fast (~1s), syspolicyd cache warm
time .venv/bin/python -c "import pandas, polars, pyarrow"

# Delete and recreate with clone (default) — slow again (~18s)
rm -rf .venv
uv venv && VIRTUAL_ENV=.venv uv pip install pandas polars pyarrow jupyterlab
time .venv/bin/python -c "import pandas, polars, pyarrow"

# Delete and recreate with hardlink — FAST (~5s)
rm -rf .venv
uv venv && VIRTUAL_ENV=.venv uv pip install --link-mode hardlink pandas polars pyarrow jupyterlab
time .venv/bin/python -c "import pandas, polars, pyarrow"
```

## Root cause

1. `uv pip install` with `--link-mode clone` (default on macOS) uses `clonefile()`, which shares storage blocks but **creates a new inode** per file
2. When Python `dlopen()`s a `.so` with an inode syspolicyd hasn't seen, it performs a full security assessment (YARA scan, code signature check)
3. Unsigned `.so` files (all pip packages) trigger `errSecCSUnsigned` (-67062) and a full scan per file
4. Results are cached per-inode — but clone gives every install new inodes, defeating the cache

With `--link-mode hardlink`, the venv's `.so` files share the inode with uv's global cache. Deleting and recreating the venv reuses the same cache archive entry → same inodes → syspolicyd sees them as already scanned.

## Evidence: hardlink vs clone comparison

Tested with `uv pip install buckaroo jupyterlab polars` (108 packages, 112 `.so` files).
Monitoring `log stream --predicate 'process == "syspolicyd"'` during each import:

```
Run                                      Time     syspolicyd lines   Sample inode
A: clone, fresh install                 19.60s    3391               13301980
B: clone, delete + reinstall            18.57s    3306               13320671  (different inode)
C: hardlink, fresh install               6.14s     175               12783585
D: hardlink, delete + reinstall          5.48s     175               12783585  (same inode)
```

Clone reinstall (B) triggers a full rescan every time — new inodes, ~3300 syspolicyd log lines, ~19s.
Hardlink reinstall (D) reuses the cache's inodes — syspolicyd sees them as already scanned, ~5s.

## Per-package breakdown

Each package tested individually in a fresh clone-mode venv (cold syspolicyd),
then immediately re-imported (warm). Delta = time attributable to syspolicyd.

```
Package         Cold      Warm     Delta    .so count   .so total size
bare python    0.04s     0.03s     0.01s       10          21.1M
polars         2.43s     0.05s     2.38s        1         147.1M
pyarrow        2.47s     0.05s     2.42s       37         105.3M

result.title: Workspace members with conflicts have empty `uv export` output
result.body:
### Summary

Workspace members that are listed in a `tools.uv.conflicts` entry with another workspace member get an empty file from running `uv export --package <member>`.

MRE:
1. Create a new uv project and cd into it: `uv init test_proj && cd test_proj`
2. Create 2 new workspace members: `uv init chronon` and `uv init thrifter`
3. Mark the two workspace members as conflicting in `pyproject.toml`:
```
[tool.uv]
conflicts = [
    [
        { package = "chronon" },
        { package = "thrifter" },
    ],
]
```

4. Add `chronon-ai` to `chronon`: `uv add --package chronon 'chronon-ai==0.0.109'`  
  (This is the latest released version of chronon, and this specific example goes away if chronon upgrades their `thrift` dependency.)
5. Add `thrift` to `thrifter`: `uv add --package thrifter 'thrift>0.15'`
6. There is now a dependency conflict between the workspace members: `chronon-ai` requires `thrift<0.14` and `thrifter` requires `thrift>0.15`.
7. Run `uv export --package chronon` and `uv export --package thrifter`. Observe the empty output for both.

For additional steps, you could add a new workspace member (`uv init safe`), add a non-conflicting dep to it (`uv add --package safe click`, for example), and then export it (`uv export --package safe`) and see it does have real output.

### Platform

Darwin 24.6.0 arm64

### Version

uv 0.10.4 (Homebrew 2026-02-17)

### Python version

Python 3.13.12

result.title: `keyring-provider = "subprocess"` not invoked on 401 — credentials never fetched for explicit private index
result.body:
### Summary

## `pyproject.toml` configuration:

```toml
[tool.uv]
keyring-provider = "subprocess"

[[tool.uv.index]]
name = "private-index"
url = "https://<domain>-<account>.d.codeartifact.<region>.amazonaws.com/pypi/<repo>/simple/"
explicit = true
authenticate = "always"

[tool.uv.sources]
my-package = { index = "private-index" }
```

## Expected behavior

When resolving a package from the private index, `uv` should call `keyring get <url> aws` via the subprocess provider before (or upon) receiving a 401, retrieve the token, and retry the request with credentials.

## Actual behavior

`uv` made the request to the index without credentials and immediately failed with `401 Unauthorized`, never invoking keyring at all. This is visible in `uv add my-package -v`:

```bash

result.title: Panic on invalid cache-control override in index config
result.body:
### Summary

`cached_client.rs` panics when a user-configured cache-control override contains characters invalid for an HTTP header value. Two sites in `CachedClient` — `send_cached_handle_stale` (line ~575) and `fresh_request` (line ~629) — call:

```rust
http::HeaderValue::from_str(header)
    .expect("Cache-Control header must be valid UTF-8")
```

`HeaderValue::from_str` rejects more than just non-UTF-8 — any byte outside the visible ASCII range plus tab causes it to fail. A user setting something like `cache-control = "max-age=3600\x01"` in their index config will crash uv instead of getting an error message.

The value comes from `IndexCacheControl` in `index.rs`, which stores it as `Option<SmallString>` with no validation at parse time.

### Platform

Linux x86_64 (code-level, platform-independent)

### Version

latest main (code read from HEAD)

result.title: Script metadata parser silently accepts duplicate script blocks
result.body:
### Summary

`ScriptTag::parse` in `uv-scripts/src/lib.rs` finds the first `# /// script` block using `FINDER.find(contents)` (line ~500) and returns its TOML. It never checks whether the file contains a second `# /// script` block after the first one closes.

PEP 723 says tools MUST error when a script contains multiple embedded metadata blocks. Right now uv silently uses whichever one comes first and ignores any others.

A file like this should be rejected:

```python
# /// script
# dependencies = ["requests"]
# ///

print("hi")

# /// script
# dependencies = ["flask"]
# ///
```

Instead uv picks `requests` and quietly drops `flask`.

### Platform

Linux x86_64 (code-level, platform-independent)

### Version

latest main (code read from HEAD)

result.title: Support resuming interrupted package downloads
result.body:
### Summary

I’d like it if file downloads (if interrupted) could resume from the exact point where they were interrupted. A similar feature is currently in place: a cache is used for files, but there’s no solution for when a file download is interrupted—it starts over from the beginning because the streaming mode is used for downloading files. This is inconvenient for people with poor internet connections, a group to which I, unfortunately, belong. I looked for an issue with the same problem, but found only one similar one in [pip repo](https://github.com/pypa/pip/issues/3128). Honestly, I'd love to see this feature, since it would make my life easier.

### Example

This feature is useful for packages like torch or tensorrt; I work with them frequently, and I find it really inconvenient that a file weighing 2.5 GiB on Windows or 900+ MB on Linux—if the download is interrupted even at 90%—doesn’t resume, but instead starts over from scratch. This takes up a lot of my time, and I think there are many people in the community who face a similar problem.

result.title: Bug: uv.lock assigns wrong source.registry to PyPI packages when a private index is configured
result.body:
### Summary

When a private index is added via [[tool.uv.index]] without explicit = true, uv sync / uv lock incorrectly records the private index URL as the source.registry for packages that were actually resolved from PyPI. The artifact download URLs (sdist, wheels) correctly point to files.pythonhosted.org, making the lockfile internally inconsistent.
This is related to #13590, but distinct: that issue involves the explicit index pattern. This issue reproduces without explicit and without [tool.uv.sources], i.e., the simpler "add a fallback private index" use case.

Example pyproject.toml
```bash
[project]
name = "uv-lock-test"
version = "0.1.0"
description = "Add your description here"
readme = "README.md"
requires-python = ">=3.13"
dependencies = [
    "python-dotenv",
    "my_package",
]

[[tool.uv.index]]
name = "myindex"
url = "https://pyhub.myindex.de/simple"
```

Relevant environment variables set at sync time:
`UV_NATIVE_TLS=true`
`UV_INDEX_MYINDEX_USERNAME=user`
`UV_INDEX_MYINDEX_PASSWORD=password`

Notes:
- `my_package` is hosted exclusively on the private index pyhub.myindex.de
- python-dotenv is a public PyPI package not present on the private index
- No explicit = true on the index; no [tool.uv.sources] block

**Steps to Reproduce**
Start from a clean state: no uv.lock, no .venv
Set environment variables as above
Run `uv sync`

**Observed Behaviour**
python-dotenv is resolved and installed correctly. However, in the generated `uv.lock`, its source.registry is set to the private index URL, while the actual download URLs point to pythonhosted.org

```bash
[[package]]
name = "python-dotenv"
version = "1.2.2"
source = { registry = "https://pyhub.myindex.de/simple" }  # ← WRONG
sdist = { url = "https://files.pythonhosted.org/packages/.../python_dotenv-1.2.2.tar.gz", ... }
wheels = [
    { url = "https://files.pythonhosted.org/packages/.../python_dotenv-1.2.2-py3-none-any.whl", ... },
]
```

The source.registry field points to the private index, but the actual artifact URLs are from PyPI/pythonhosted, the package was clearly fetched from PyPI, not from the private registry.

*Expected Behaviour*
python-dotenv should have source = { registry = "https://pypi.org/simple" } in the lockfile, since it was resolved from PyPI and its artifacts are hosted there.

*Why This Matters / Potential Impact*
The lockfile is semantically incorrect and misleading
This is a silent correctness issue, the install may succeed locally, but the lockfile diverges from reality

### Platform

WSL Ubuntu 

### Version

uv 0.10.12 (x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu)

### Python version

3.13.10

result.title: `uv` fails to sync remote package with local dependency
result.body:
### Summary

## Explanation
I have a library that I use in several other packages, and mostly use it as a local dependency while developing on branches. However, recently on a new package I'm finding that while syncing a dependency from git that has the local one as another dependency it fails as follws:
```sh
$ uv sync
    Updated ssh://<EMAIL_1>/proj/dep01.git (ff49cf978bff24c76f4afb32d8df09c712a6cfbb) # --> No dependency of loca package
    Updated ssh://<EMAIL_1>/proj/dep02.git (30dcc71701572ccbe1c1dc02be61b53e01d1cde9) # --> Has dependency
    × Failed to download and build `fpga @ git+ssh://<EMAIL_1>/proj/dep02.git@branch#subdirectory=../lib/fpga`
  ╰─▶ The source distribution `git+ssh://<EMAIL_1>/proj/dep02.git@branch#subdirectory=../lib/fpga` has no subdirectory `../lib/fpga`
```
## Expected behavior
`uv sync` resolves the dependency as local, instead of searching the remote.
--------
Note: The mentioned library `fpga` is also a dependency of the current package where I'm adding `dep02`.

## Structure
```
../
├─ lib/
│  ├─ fpga/
│  │  ├─ pyproject.toml
├─ dep01/
│  ├─ pyproject.toml
├─ dep02/
│  ├─ pyproject.toml
├─ cur_pkg/
│  ├─ pyproject.toml
```

I'm running `uv sync` inside `cur_pkg`. I can install `fpga` fine with `uv pip`.

### Platform

Fedora 43

### Version

uv 0.10.8

### Python version

Python 3.13.9

result.title: `uv run --preview-features=target-workspace-discovery` fails needlessly reading `uv.toml`, `pyproject.toml` from inaccessible cwd
result.body:
### Summary

```console
$ uv init /tmp/project
$ uv --project=/tmp/project add requests
$ echo 'import requests; print(requests.__version__)' > /tmp/project/main.py
$ mkdir /tmp/elsewhere
$ cd /tmp/elsewhere
$ uv run --preview-features=target-workspace-discovery /tmp/project/main.py
2.32.5
$ chmod 000 .
$ uv run --preview-features=target-workspace-discovery /tmp/project/main.py
error: failed to open file `/tmp/elsewhere/uv.toml`: Permission denied (os error 13)
```

This comes up when an administrator with cwd `/root` uses `su` to run a script as another user who can’t read `/root`. For example, a Zulip administrator [expects](https://zulip.readthedocs.io/en/latest/production/export-and-import.html#backups) to be able to run `su zulip -c '/home/zulip/deployments/current/manage.py backup'`.

(Rereported from https://github.com/astral-sh/uv/issues/11302#issuecomment-3857347181 with a more streamlined test case.)

Please merge this fix:

- #17890

### Platform

Linux amd64

### Version

0.11.0

### Python version

Python 3.14.3

**Triage for astral-sh/uv#18687**

The issue: with `--preview-features=target-workspace-discovery`, `uv run` fails with "Permission denied" when the current directory is unreadable (for example `chmod 000 .`). - `bug`: this is incorrect behavior.
- `area:workspaces`: the problem is in workspace/project discovery.
- `area:configuration`: the failure comes from reading `uv.toml` and `pyproject.toml`.
- `preview`: the bug only occurs behind the `target-workspace-discovery` preview flag.

**Duplicate check:** The search found no earlier issue reporting this same failure. The reporter links #11302, which is closed and covers the feature that introduced the cwd-vs-script-directory discovery. That is related context, not the same bug, so I did not mark this as a duplicate.

**Draft reply:** Drafted (not posted). It thanks the reporter, acknowledges the reproduction, says the issue is queued for triage and that PR #17890 will be reviewed. It makes no promises about fixes or timelines.

- Labels: `bug`, `area:workspaces`, `area:configuration`, `preview`
- Duplicate: no
- Related: #11302 (closed predecessor), PR #17890 (proposed fix, referenced by the reporter)

result.title: UV `11.0` flash-attn incompatibility
result.body:
### Summary

I have configured flash attention as described in https://docs.astral.sh/uv/concepts/projects/config/#augmenting-build-dependencies
```toml
[project]
name = "uvflash"
version = "0.1.0"
description = "Add your description here"
readme = "README.md"
requires-python = ">=3.14"
dependencies = [
    "torch>=2.11.0",
]

[project.optional-dependencies]
flash_attention = ["flash-attn>=2.6.3"]

[tool.uv.extra-build-dependencies]
flash-attn = [{ requirement = "torch", match-runtime = true }]
```

And when I try `uv sync` I get error

```
  × Failed to download and build `flash-attn==2.8.3`
  ╰─▶ Extra build requirement `torch` was declared with `match-runtime = true`, but `flash-attn` does not declare static metadata, making runtime-matching impossible
  help: `flash-attn` (v2.8.3) was included because `uvflash[flash-attention]` (v0.1.0) depends on `flash-attn>=2.6.3`
```
But on `uv<0.11.0` this worked correctly

### Platform

mac, ubuntu, any

### Version

0.11.0

### Python version

any

result.title: `uvx run package_name` downloads and tries to run the package `run`
result.body:
### Summary

The correct command to run a tool with `uvx` is `uvx command` (i.e., `uvx ruff`). However, since `run` is used in other contexts (i.e., `uv run` inside a repository), `uvx run command` is a common typo. When the user runs `uvx run command`, uv downloads and (tries to) run the package run (which fails, since that package provides no executables). The package run is a very small, recent (first commit is from last december), and it seems safe to say that most of the times when the user runs `uvx run command` they didn't want mean the project run.

Due to `run` being used by `uv` in other contexts, `uvx run` should alert the user and ask for confirmation.

### Example

```
C:\Temp\teste>uvx --verbose run ruff
(...)
DEBUG Searching for a compatible version of run (*)
DEBUG Selecting: run==0.3 [compatible] (run-0.3-py3-none-any.whl)
(...)
```

### Platform

Windows

### Version

uvx 0.10.11 (006b56b 2026-03-16)

### Python version

Python 3.14.0

result.title: uv exclude-newer for cooldown: Stop writing timestamp in uv.lock to avoid git conflicts
result.body:
### Summary

(I've tried searching for a similar issue, and read the original issue for dependency cooldown. Didn't see a discussion of this.)

Setting a cooldown in `pyproject.toml`, like `1 week` for instance, also writes a timestamp into `uv.lock`. When upgrading a package, the timestamp gets updated.

The problem comes with larger teams working on the same code base, in multiple branches. If a package is updated in one branch, and a different package is upgraded in a separate branch, you have a merge conflict, since they both write (different) timestamps.

If `uv` _only_ wrote the span in the lock file, that would avoid merge conflicts.

Example:
```bash
git switch -c exclude-newer-base
# add exclude-newer = "1 week" to pyproject.toml
uv lock
git add -u && git commit -m "add exclude-newer cooldown"

git switch -c exclude-newer-1
uv lock -P ruff && git add -u && git commit -m "upgrade ruff"

git switch exclude-newer-base
git switch -c exclude-newer-2
uv lock -P ruff && git add -u && git commit -m "upgrade ruff"

git switch exclude-newer-base
git merge exclude-newer-1    # fast-forward
git merge exclude-newer-2    # merge conflict in uv.lock
```

triage.draft_reply:
Thanks for the detailed report! This comes from uv's default index behavior. When a package is available on more than one index, uv only considers versions from the first index that contains it, to guard against dependency confusion. pip instead merges versions from all indexes, which is why the same requirements file resolves with pip but not with uv.

In your case, `torchcodec` is found on `https://download.pytorch.org/whl/cu128`, but none of the versions there have a `win_amd64` wheel that matches the requirement, so uv stops there. The error hint points to the fix: `--index-strategy unsafe-best-match`, which lets uv consider versions from every index. You mentioned you'd rather keep the change minimal, so this is a tradeoff: that flag is the closest match to pip's behavior, but it does relax the first-index protection, so it's only appropriate if you trust both indexes.

Hope that helps you get unblocked.

args.body:
Thanks for the detailed report! This comes from uv's default index behavior. When a package is available on more than one index, uv only considers versions from the first index that contains it, to guard against dependency confusion. pip instead merges versions from all indexes, which is why the same requirements file resolves with pip but not with uv.

In your case, `torchcodec` is found on `https://download.pytorch.org/whl/cu128`, but none of the versions there have a `win_amd64` wheel that matches the requirement, so uv stops there. The error hint points to the fix: `--index-strategy unsafe-best-match`, which lets uv consider versions from every index. You mentioned you'd rather keep the change minimal, so this is a tradeoff: that flag is the closest match to pip's behavior, but it does relax the first-index protection, so it's only appropriate if you trust both indexes.

Hope that helps you get unblocked.

I installed uv using the following command:
curl -LsSf https://astral.sh/uv/install.sh | sh

I would like to completely remove it from my system. Since the installer script doesn't seem to have an uninstall flag, what is the recommended way to perform a clean manual uninstall?

Based on the installer's behavior, I assume I need to:
Delete the binaries (e.g., in ~/.local/bin/uv).
Remove the config folder (e.g., ~/.config/uv).
Clean up my shell profile (.bashrc / .zshrc).

Debian 13

uv 0.10.12 (x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu)

Here are the places uv typically stores data, which you can check on your system:

- **Binaries:** `uv` and `uvx`, usually in `~/.local/bin` (run `which uv uvx` to confirm).
- **Cache:** run `uv cache dir` to find it. You can also run `uv cache clean` before removing the binaries.
- **Installed Python versions:** run `uv python dir`. These are managed by uv and can be large.
- **Installed tools:** run `uv tool dir`, which holds tools installed with `uv tool install`.

result.body:
### Summary

As of 0.11.0, you could install UV into a venv:
```
 C:\Users\1\AppData\Roaming\Python\Python312\Scripts\uv.exe pip install uv -p .\venv12\Scripts\python.exe
```
This would create `venv12/Scripts/uv.exe` which could then be used to install packages in the venv, so that the `-p` argument could be omitted and the venv need not be activated.

As of 0.11.1, this no longer happens (and breaks my installation scripts)

Windows

0.11.1

Python 3.12.4

Hello,

I am trying to have an project the keyring authentication to access a dependency that is in a private gcloud artifact registry. I followed the following instructions:

https://docs.cloud.google.com/artifact-registry/docs/python/authentication 
https://docs.astral.sh/uv/guides/integration/google/#authenticate-with-keyring-and-keyringsgoogle-artifactregistry-auth

In my pyproject.toml I have:

```
dependencies=[
    [...],
    private-package==2.18.1
]

[...]

[tool.uv.sources]
private-package = { index = "private-artifacts" }

[[tool.uv.index]]
name = "private-artifacts"
url = "https://<EMAIL_1>/private-project/private-artifacts/simple/"
explicit = true
```

When I run `uv sync` or `uv sync --keyring-profider=subprocess`, I get:
```
Resolved 183 packages in 2ms
  x Failed to download `private-package==2.18.1`
  |-> Failed to fetch: `https://europe-west9-python.pkg.dev/private-project/private-artifacts/private-package/private-package-2.18.1-cp313-cp313-win_amd64.whl`
  `-> HTTP status client error (401 Unauthorized) for url

  help: `private-package` (v2.18.1) was included because `my-project` (v1.1.0) depends on `private-package`
```

I have run `gcloud auth login`  succesfully  and installed the keyring providers:
```
$ keyring --list-backends
keyring.backends.Windows.WinVaultKeyring (priority: 5)
keyring.backends.fail.Keyring (priority: 0)
keyrings.gauth.GooglePythonAuth (priority: 9)
keyring.backends.chainer.ChainerBackend (priority: 10)
```

If I use the authentication through the access token, using the `UV_INDEX_PRIVATE_ARTIFACTS_PASSWORD` things work.
But I would like the keyring to handle the token management instead.

Am I missing anything else in the setup? Either locally or in gcould services?

Thanks

Windows 11 x64

uv 0.11.1 (a6042f67f 2026-03-24 x86_64-pc-windows-msvc)

args.body:
Thanks for the detailed report! A few things that would help us narrow this down:

1. The command in your report is `uv sync --keyring-profider=subprocess`, which looks like a typo. The flag is `--keyring-provider=subprocess` (or set `UV_KEYRING_PROVIDER=subprocess`). Could you confirm the correct spelling was used when you saw the 401?
2. Could you run `uv sync -v` (or `--verbose`) and share the output, with any tokens or project-specific URLs redacted? It should show whether uv is querying the keyring for the index and what happens with that lookup.
3. Could you run `keyring get https://europe-west9-python.pkg.dev/private-project/private-artifacts/simple/ oauth2accesstoken` directly in the same shell? That tells us whether the keyring backend can return a credential for that URL on its own.

Once we have that, we can see whether this is a uv configuration issue or something in the keyring setup.

## Triage for astral-sh/uv#18723

**Summary:** The reporter (on Windows 11, uv 0.11.1) can't get uv to use the keyring-based Google Artifact Registry credentials for a private index. `uv sync` fails with a 401 when downloading a private package. Using an access token through `UV_INDEX_PRIVATE_ARTIFACTS_PASSWORD` works, so the index and package are fine. The question is why the keyring lookup isn't providing the credential.

**Suggested labels:**
- `question`: the reporter is asking for help with setup.
- `area:authentication`: keyring and credential handling.
- `area:registry`: private index access.
- `area:windows`: the reporter is on Windows, and the keyring backend setup is Windows-specific.

**Duplicates:** None marked. The closest matches are #7003 (`uv add keyring` breaks private index auth), #16402 (private index auth fails for `uv sync`), #12716 (private packages from Google Artifact Registry, closed), and #17144 (401 with keyring on Azure DevOps). Each covers part of the problem, but none is clearly the same report, so I didn't mark it as a duplicate. A maintainer should compare #12716 and #16402 in particular.

**Draft reply (not posted):** Asks the reporter to:
1. Check the flag spelling. The report shows `--keyring-profider`, which should be `--keyring-provider`.
2. Share `uv sync -v` output with secrets redacted.
3. Run `keyring get` for the index URL with `oauth2accesstoken` to confirm the keyring backend can return a credential on its own.

**Notes for maintainers:**
- The reporter's `keyring --list-backends` output shows `keyrings.gauth.GooglePythonAuth` at priority 9, below the chainer at 10. Whether that matters is unclear, and the verbose output should help.
- I did not promise a fix or timeline in the draft.

result.title: `uvx` doesn't seem to work with local project with defined scripts
result.body:
### Question

Hello!

As in the title. I can't seem to get `uvx` to work with a local project that has scripts defined in the `pyproject.toml` file. Here's the config:

```toml
[project]
name = "notely"
version = "0.1.0"
description = "Add your description here"
readme = "README.md"
requires-python = ">=3.14"
scripts.notely = "notely.main:main"
dependencies = [
    "markdown-it-py>=4.0.0",
    "markdownify>=1.2.2",
    "nicegui>=3.9.0",
    "pyyaml>=6.0.3",
    "rich-click>=1.9.7",
]

[dependency-groups]
dev = [
    ...
]
lint = [
    "ruff>=0.15.4",
]

[build-system]
requires = ["hatchling"]
build-backend = "hatchling.build"

[tool.hatch.build.targets.wheel]
packages = [ "notely" ]

...
```

When I run `uvx --from . notely`, I'm getting:

```
Package `notely` does not provide any executables.
```

Apologies if this is not the right place to ask, and thank you kindly for the help!

### Platform

Windows 11 x86_64

### Version

uv 0.8.22 (ade2bdbd2 2025-09-23)

It concerns adding a summary to the JSON output, not the missing JSON on the `--check` failure path, so I did not mark this as a duplicate. A maintainer may want to look at it for context.

**Draft reply:** Drafted with `draft_comment` but not posted. It thanks the reporter, says the JSON output is missing only when `--check` finds an outdated environment, and notes that a maintainer will follow up. It makes no promises about fixes or timelines.

**Final triage:** Label as `bug`, `area:json-output`, `area:projects`. Not a duplicate. Review and post the drafted reply.

result.title: Cannot install debug wheels into debug CPython venv
result.body:
### Summary

## Summary

Since version 0.10.0 and last verified with 0.11.2, uv refuses to install debug wheels into a venv with a debug CPython. This appears to be a regression compared with uv 0.9.30.

In slightly more detail:
* Using uv to create a venv with a CPython debug build works.
* Using uv to build a wheel of a native package works.
* Installing a debug wheel built by uv into a project venv that uses a CPython debug build does NOT work.

## Steps to reproduce

### Preparation

Use the following tarball for a trivial native package:

[native_demo-0.1.0.tar.gz](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/26346629/native_demo-0.1.0.tar.gz)

Mount or copy this into a docker container running `ghcr.io/astral-sh/uv:debian`.
Then inside the running container:
```
apt update -qq && apt install -y python3-dbg python3-dev
uv venv --python /usr/bin/python3-dbg   # Important: debug build
. .venv/bin/activate
```
So far so good.

### Action

Expected: uv can build and install the native package.

Observed: installation fails. Details:
```
# uv pip install /tmp/native_demo-0.1.0.tar.gz
Using Python 3.13.5 environment at: /root/.venv
Resolved 1 package in 20ms
      Built native-demo @ file:///tmp/native_demo-0.1.0.tar.gz
  x Failed to build `native-demo @ file:///tmp/native_demo-0.1.0.tar.gz`
  `-> The built wheel `native_demo-0.1.0-cp313-cp313d-linux_x86_64.whl` is not compatible with the current Python 3.13
      on manylinux x86_64
```

If we dig into it, we see that the wheel build succeeds, but the install fails:
```
# uv build --wheel /tmp/native_demo-0.1.0.tar.gz
[snip]
Successfully built /tmp/native_demo-0.1.0-cp313-cp313d-linux_x86_64.whl

# uv pip install /tmp/native_demo-0.1.0-cp313-cp313d-linux_x86_64.whl
Using Python 3.13.5 environment at: /root/.venv
Resolved 1 package in 15ms
error: Failed to determine installation plan
  Caused by: A path dependency is incompatible with the current platform: /tmp/native_demo-0.1.0-cp313-cp313d-linux_x86_64.whl

hint: The wheel is compatible with CPython 3.13 (`cp313d`), but you're using CPython 3.13 (`cp313`)
```

### Platform

Docker image ghcr.io/astral-sh/uv:debian running on Linux 6.8.0-94-generic x86_64 GNU/Linux

### Version

0.11.2 (also reproducible with 0.10 onwards)

### Python version

Important: a DEBUG build of CPython; in this case 3.13.5

triage.draft_reply:
Thanks for the detailed report! The error suggests uv is still seeing an older cached copy of the `requests` index page for PyPI, even though 2.33.1 is now published.

Could you try clearing the cache entry for that package and retrying?

```bash
uv cache clean requests
uv pip install "requests>=2.33.0"
```

Or, to bypass the cache for a single run:

```bash
uv pip install --refresh-package requests "requests>=2.33.0"
```

If that still fails, could you share the output of `uv pip install -v "requests>=2.33.0"` (with any sensitive URLs redacted)? Also let us know whether `uv` is configured with any extra indexes (`--index-url`, `--extra-index-url`, or `[[tool.uv.index]]`), since that affects which index is consulted first.

result.body:
### Summary

Hello uv team,

As of last week, a new version of the package requests is available at https://pypi.org/project/requests. I tried to install it with uv but I am getting the below error:

```bash
❯ uv pip install "requests>=2.33.0"

      hint: `requests` was found on https://pypi.org/simple, but not at the requested version (requests>=2.33.0). A compatible version may be available on a subsequent index (e.g., https://pypi.org/simple).
      By default, uv will only consider versions that are published on the first index that contains a given package, to avoid dependency confusion attacks. If all indexes are equally trusted, use
      `--index-strategy unsafe-best-match` to consider all versions from all indexes, regardless of the order in which they were defined.
```

I also tried the below commands without success:

```bash
uv sync --upgrade-package requests # nothing happens
uv sync # after adding requests>=2.33.0 in the dependencies section of my pyproject.toml, fails with the same error message as above

The package is indeed available on the index. Could you help please?

Thank you in advance for considering my request.

result.title: `uv venv` recommends use of `source` in incompatible shells
result.body:
### Summary

`uv venv` suggests sourcing the virtual environment with `source` regardless of whether the current shell supports `source`. `source` is not POSIX-compliant, and not provided by many commonly available shells such as `ash` and `dash`. The POSIX-compliant instruction is `. .venv/bin/activate`.

On Ubuntu, or a system with `dash` manually installed:

```shell
$ dash
$ uv venv .venv
Using CPython 3.11.15
Creating virtual environment at: .venv
Activate with: source .venv/bin/activate
$ source .venv/bin/activate
dash: 8: source: not found
$ . .venv/bin/activate
(.venv) $ 
```

### Platform

e..g. Ubuntu, Alpine

### Version

uv 0.11.1 (x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu)

### Python version

3.11 / whatever

result.title: Mismatching hash is ignored when dependency is direct url
result.body:
### Summary

Given the following `pyproject.toml` file:

```toml
[project]
name = "pylock"
version = "0.1.0"
requires-python = ">=3.10"
dependencies = [
    "protobug @ https://files.pythonhosted.org/packages/f2/cc/db26b91cddffbcf0c6df7834fd642578f737fe34197635ae8ea64643a35f/protobug-0.3.0-py3-none-any.whl#sha256=ee81583f376bb38e5e7af425d2453e5e8d4b57bfbf45e5dba1a75329c2026520",
]
```

When installing using `uv pip install .`, it ignores the mismatching hash of the dependency:
```shell
$ uv venv --clear
Using CPython 3.14.1
Creating virtual environment at: .venv
Activate with: source .venv/bin/activate

$ source .venv/bin/activate

$ uv --no-config --no-cache pip install .
Resolved 2 packages in 37ms
      Built pylock @ file:///home/simon/source/private/pylock
Prepared 2 packages in 655ms
Installed 2 packages in 5ms
 + protobug==0.3.0 (from https://files.pythonhosted.org/packages/f2/cc/db26b91cddffbcf0c6df7834fd642578f737fe34197635ae8ea64643a35f/protobug-0.3.0-py3-none-any.whl#sha256=ee81583f376bb38e5e7af425d2453e5e8d4b57bfbf45e5dba1a75329c2026520)
 + pylock==0.1.0 (from file:///home/simon/source/private/pylock)
```

This behavior is different from how `pip` behaves:

```shell
$ uv venv --clear --seed
Using CPython 3.14.1
Creating virtual environment at: .venv
Activate with: source .venv/bin/activate

$ source .venv/bin/activate
$ pip install .
Processing ./.
  Installing build dependencies ... done
  Getting requirements to build wheel ... done
  Preparing metadata (pyproject.toml) ... done
Collecting protobug @ https://files.pythonhosted.org/packages/f2/cc/db26b91cddffbcf0c6df7834fd642578f737fe34197635ae8ea64643a35f/protobug-0.3.0-py3-none-any.whl#sha256=ee81583f376bb38e5e7af425d2453e5e8d4b57bfbf45e5dba1a75329c2026520 (from pylock==0.1.0)
  Downloading protobug-0.3.0-py3-none-any.whl (11 kB)
ERROR: THESE PACKAGES DO NOT MATCH THE HASHES FROM THE REQUIREMENTS FILE. If you have updated the package versions, please update the hashes. Otherwise, examine the package contents carefully; someone may have tampered with them.
    protobug @ https://files.pythonhosted.org/packages/f2/cc/db26b91cddffbcf0c6df7834fd642578f737fe34197635ae8ea64643a35f/protobug-0.3.0-py3-none-any.whl#sha256=ee81583f376bb38e5e7af425d2453e5e8d4b57bfbf45e5dba1a75329c2026520 from https://files.pythonhosted.org/packages/f2/cc/db26b91cddffbcf0c6df7834fd642578f737fe34197635ae8ea64643a35f/protobug-0.3.0-py3-none-any.whl#sha256=ee81583f376bb38e5e7af425d2453e5e8d4b57bfbf45e5dba1a75329c2026520 (from pylock==0.1.0):
        Expected sha256 ee81583f376bb38e5e7af425d2453e5e8d4b57bfbf45e5dba1a75329c2026520
             Got        ee81583f376bb38e5e7af425d2453e5e8d4b57bfbf45e5dba1a75329c202652e
```

If you `uv pip install` the url dependency directly, you get the expected error:

```shell
$ uv venv --clear
Using CPython 3.14.1
Creating virtual environment at: .venv
Activate with: source .venv/bin/activate

$ uv pip install "protobug @ https://files.pythonhosted.org/packages/f2/cc/db26b91cddffbcf0c6df7834fd642578f737fe34197635ae8ea64643a35f/protobug-0.3.0-py3-none-any.whl#sha256=ee81583f376bb38e5e7af425d2453e5e8d4b57bfbf45e5dba1a75329c2026520"
Resolved 1 package in 40ms
  × Failed to download `protobug @ https://files.pythonhosted.org/packages/f2/cc/db26b91cddffbcf0c6df7834fd642578f737fe34197635ae8ea64643a35f/protobug-0.3.0-py3-none-any.whl#sha256=ee81583f376bb38e5e7af425d2453e5e8d4b57bfbf45e5dba1a75329c2026520`

      Expected:
        sha256:ee81583f376bb38e5e7af425d2453e5e8d4b57bfbf45e5dba1a75329c2026520

**Summary:** The reporter ran `uv cache prune` (uv 0.11.2, Linux, Ubuntu 24.04), which reported removing 714,036 files (85.8 GiB). `df` afterward shows `/home` still at 99% with only about 60G free, so they estimate only about 45G was actually freed.

Related but distinct open issues include #16008 (prune should delete unused packages based on link count) and #15569 (`cache clean`/`prune` fails with os error 63). Neither reports the same problem, so I didn't mark this as a duplicate.

**Likely cause:** I suspect hard links. uv links cache files into virtual environments, so removing a cache entry doesn't free its blocks while a venv still references them. The reported "removed" total may count files that still use disk space. Concurrent writes to the same filesystem could also explain some of the gap. This is a hypothesis, not confirmed.

**Draft reply:** I drafted a friendly comment (not posted) that explains the hard-link possibility and asks for:
- `uv cache dir` and `du -sh` output before and after the prune,
- whether the cache and the virtual environments share a filesystem,

result.title: Reject locked malware installations
result.body:
If the user's `uv.lock` contains a version that is known to be malicious, then we should reject its installation. 

This is slightly different from what `uv audit` does -- `uv audit` principally checks from known vulnerabilities, not malware or compromised packages. The latter is reported via a distinct "stream" on OSV (`MAL-` reports).

I need to think a bit more about the design here/implications.

- [x] Support filtering by malware (`MAL-`) in the OSV client: https://github.com/astral-sh/uv/pull/18934
- [x] Fetch `MAL-` entries during lockfile installation and reject the install if we have any: https://github.com/astral-sh/uv/pull/18936
- [x] Cache `MAL-` lookups: #19038

result.title: Enable opt out of exclude_newer for trusted package sources to enable use of AWS CodeArtifact
result.body:
### Summary

I have tried to enable `exclude_newer` in a repo that sources packages from both PyPI and a private AWS CodeArtifact source. I am doing this to mitigate risks associated with recent supply chain attacks, I believe this is a common use of this feature.

Unfortunately because the [AWS CodeArtifact API](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/codeartifact/latest/ug/python-compatibility.html) does not support the required date time publishing meta data, uv cannot resolve the dependencies. I do not need `exclude_newer` applied here because the packages in this package store are always older than my `exclude_newer` setting. I believe others will be in a similar situation. 

**Suggestion:** Allow some sources to be exempt from this setting. 



### Example


Example error I get for a CodeArtifact package when running `uv lock`
```
× No solution found when resolving dependencies for split (markers:
  │ python_full_version == '3.12.*' and sys_platform == 'linux'):
  ╰─▶ Because xxxx==zzzz has no publish time and pipelines depends on
      xxxx==zzzz, we can conclude that pipelines's requirements are
      unsatisfiable.
      And because your workspace requires pipelines, we can conclude that your
      workspace's requirements are unsatisfiable.

      hint: The resolution failed for an environment that is not the current one,
      consider limiting the environments with `tool.uv.environments`.
```

result.title: Dependencies pinned to an index are still searched on pypi
result.body:
### Summary

With a project file looking like `pyproject.toml`:

```toml
[project]
name = "test-pin"
version = "0.1.0"
description = "Add your description here"
readme = "README.md"
requires-python = ">=3.9.2"
dependencies = []

[tool.uv.sources]
pkgDepA = { index = "privpi" }
pkgDepB = { index = "privpi" }
pkgMain= { index = "privpi" }

[[tool.uv.index]]
name = "privpi"
url = "https://pypi.private.com/simple/"
explicit = true
```

The package `pkgMain` has the two other packages as dependencies, the `pkgMain` is retrieved from the private index but the dependencies are searched on the pypi index resulting in failure.

```
$ uv add -v pkgMain
[...]
  × No solution found when resolving dependencies:
  ╰─▶ Because pkgDepA was not found in the package registry and pkgDepA was not found in the package
      registry, we can conclude that pkgDepA>=0.0.7,<0.0.12 cannot be used.
      And because pkgMain<=0.1.68 depends on pkgDepA>=0.0.7 and only the following versions of pkgMain are
      available:
          pkgMain==0.1.65
          pkgMain==0.1.66
          pkgMain==0.1.67
          pkgMain==0.1.68
          pkgMain==0.1.69
          pkgMain==0.1.70
          pkgMain==0.1.71
          pkgMain==0.1.72
          pkgMain==0.1.73
          pkgMain==0.1.74
          pkgMain==0.1.75
          pkgMain==0.1.76
      we can conclude that pkgMain<0.1.69 cannot be used. (1)

      Because pkgDepA was not found in the package registry and pkgDepA was not found in the package
      registry, we can conclude that pkgDepA>=0.0.11 cannot be used.
      And because pkgMain==0.1.69 depends on pkgDepA>=0.0.11, we can conclude that pkgMain==0.1.69 cannot
      be used.
      And because we know from (1) that pkgMain<0.1.69 cannot be used, we can conclude that pkgMain<0.1.70 cannot be
      used. (2)

      Because pkgDepA was not found in the package registry and pkgMain>=0.1.70 depends on
      pkgDepA>=0.0.12, we can conclude that pkgMain>=0.1.70 cannot be used.
      And because we know from (2) that pkgMain<0.1.70 cannot be used, we can conclude that all versions of pkgMain
      cannot be used.
      And because your project depends on pkgMain, we can conclude that your project's requirements are
      unsatisfiable.
  help: If you want to add the package regardless of the failed resolution, provide the `--frozen` flag to skip
        locking and syncing.
```

If I use `uv add pkgDepA` or `uv add pkgdepB`, everything works properly and the packages are retrieved from the private index.

I haven't found another issue describing the same problem.

### Platform

Linux Mint 22.3

### Version

uv 0.9.18

### Python version

python 3.9.2

result.title: Cargo fails to build uv-build from a source distribution with `--locked`
result.body:
### Summary

The Cargo.lock file that's generated with for the `uv-build` source distribution is out of date from Cargo.toml.

- From `crates/uv-build`: `maturin sdist`
- `tar zxf ../../target/wheels/uv_build-0.11.3.tar.gz && cd uv_build-0.11.3 && cargo build --locked`

```
error: cannot update the lock file [...]/uv/crates/uv-build/uv_build-0.11.3/Cargo.lock because --locked was passed to prevent this
help: to generate the lock file without accessing the network, remove the --locked flag and use --offline instead.
```

`cargo vendor --locked` is similar:

```
error: failed to sync

Caused by:
  failed to load lockfile for [...]/uv/crates/uv-build/uv_build-0.11.3

Caused by:
  cannot update the lock file [...]/uv/crates/uv-build/uv_build-0.11.3/Cargo.lock because --locked was passed to prevent this
  help: to generate the lock file without accessing the network, remove the --locked flag and use --offline instead.
```

`cargo build` or `cargo generate-lockfile` work, but then the build is non-deterministic.

### Platform

Linux

### Version

0.11.3

### Python version

3.14.3

result.title: uv run --locked --script does not fail when .lock file is missing
result.body:
### Summary

I'm trying to use uv to prevent supply chain attacks on my scripts.

I use something like this (in a `.py` file):
```
#!/usr/bin/env -S uv run --locked --script
# /// script
# requires-python = "..."
# dependencies = [
...
# ]
# ///
```

What I've noticed is that if the corresponding `.lock` file does not exist, `uv` just presents a warning and installs the NEWEST version of all packages.
`warning: No lockfile found for Python script (ignoring `--locked`); run `uv lock --script` to generate a lockfile`

This defeats the point of using --locked at all.

This page: https://docs.astral.sh/uv/concepts/projects/sync/

says: "To disable automatic locking, use the --locked option:"

But it does not disable automatic locking, it only disables it *if a lockfile is found*.

I think more secure behaviour would be for `--locked` to use the contents of the lockfile, if the file is empty or not present, either fail or print a warning about an empty lockfile and just install nothing (which would almost certainly cause the python script to ultimately fail, but at least the warning would give a clue to devs what's going on).

### Platform

Linux 6.18.5-100.fc42.x86_64 x86_64 GNU/Linux (Fedora 42)

### Version

uv 0.11.3 (x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu)

### Python version

Python 3.13.12

### Summary

According to the docs, `exclude-newer` should support duration strings:

> Accepts RFC 3339 timestamps (e.g., 2006-12-02T02:07:43Z), a "friendly" duration (e.g., 24 hours, 1 week, 30 days), or an ISO 8601 duration (e.g., PT24H, P7D, P30D).

However, none of the duration forms works with `UV_EXCLUDE_NEWER`. The below test script yields the following output:

```
cat >test-uv-exclude-newer.sh <<EOF
#!/usr/bin/env bash

# Reproduce: UV_EXCLUDE_NEWER rejects friendly and ISO 8601 durations
# despite https://docs.astral.sh/uv/reference/settings/#exclude-newer
# documenting them as accepted.

uv --version
echo ""

set -x

UV_EXCLUDE_NEWER='7 days'  uvx ministack --version
UV_EXCLUDE_NEWER='1 week'  uvx ministack --version
UV_EXCLUDE_NEWER='24 hours' uvx ministack --version
UV_EXCLUDE_NEWER='P7D'     uvx ministack --version
UV_EXCLUDE_NEWER='PT24H'   uvx ministack --version
UV_EXCLUDE_NEWER='2026-04-01' uvx ministack --version
EOF

result.title: Does uv support ROCM7.2 dependency management through pyproject.toml
result.body:
### Question

I followed the instructions here:

https://docs.astral.sh/uv/guides/integration/pytorch/#installing-pytorch

I setup my pyproject.toml for ROCM6.4, and everything resolves fine and I can do AI model loading and inferencing.


Here it is for reference:

```
[project]
name = "myllmsandbox"
version = "0.1.1"
description = "Basic Sandbox for testing out AI LLM functionality, specficially using the huggingface.co tooling"
readme = "README.md"
requires-python = ">=3.13"
dependencies = [
    "pip>=26.0.1",
    "sounddevice>=0.5.5",
    "soundfile>=0.13.1",

    "transformers>=5.5.0",
    "accelerate>=1.13.0",
    "torch>=2.9.1",
    "torchaudio>=2.9.1",
    "torchvision>=0.24.1",
    "pytorch-triton-rocm>=3.5.1; sys_platform == 'linux'",
]

[tool.uv.sources]
torch = [
  { index = "pytorch-rocm", marker = "sys_platform == 'linux'" },
]
torchaudio = [
  { index = "pytorch-rocm", marker = "sys_platform == 'linux'" },
]
torchvision = [
  { index = "pytorch-rocm", marker = "sys_platform == 'linux'" },
]
pytorch-triton-rocm = [
  { index = "pytorch-rocm", marker = "sys_platform == 'linux'" },
]

[[tool.uv.index]]
name = "pytorch-rocm"
url = "https://download.pytorch.org/whl/rocm6.4"
explicit = true
```


I decided to upgrade to ROCM7.2.  

- I replaced url in tool.uv.index to: https://download.pytorch.org/whl/rocm7.2/
- I removed all references to pytorch-triton-rocm as well, as I think ROCM7+ does not need it.

When I run _uv sync_, I get:

  _× No solution found when resolving dependencies for split (markers: python_full_version >= '3.13' and sys_platform == 'linux'):
  ╰─▶ Because there is no version of triton-rocm{sys_platform == 'linux'}==3.6.0 and torch==2.11.0+rocm7.2 depends on triton-rocm{sys_platform == 'linux'}==3.6.0, we can conclude that torch==2.11.0+rocm7.2 cannot be used.
      And because only the following versions of torch{sys_platform == 'linux'} are available:
          torch{sys_platform == 'linux'}<2.9.1
          torch{sys_platform == 'linux'}==2.11.0+rocm7.2
      and your project depends on torch{sys_platform == 'linux'}>=2.9.1, we can conclude that your project's requirements are unsatisfiable._


I realize I may be premature here since ROCM support for 7.2 was just added, but I tried the same exercise with ROCM7.1 and ROCM7.0, and got similar errors.

Is there something that I am missing here, with large changes between ROCM6x and ROCM7x, or something with how uv will support using pytorch with ROCM moving forward?



### Platform

Arch Linux x86_64

### Version

0.11.3

result.title: exclude-newer: allow exempting packages with no upload date
result.body:
## Problem

When using `exclude-newer` with a private PyPI registry (Sonatype Nexus), packages that lack upload timestamps are rejected even when `exclude-newer-package` is set for them.

Nexus doesn't emit upload dates in its simple API responses. Setting `exclude-newer-package = { my-pkg = "2099-01-01" }` doesn't help — uv still reports "has no publish time" and excludes the package.

## Current behavior

```
× No solution found when resolving dependencies for split (markers: python_full_version >= '3.14'):
╰─▶ Because loee-commons==0.8.0 has no publish time and there are no versions of loee-commons,
    we can conclude that loee-commons>=0.8.0,<1 cannot be used.
```

## Expected behavior

When `exclude-newer-package` is set for a package, packages with no upload date should be treated as allowed (the user has explicitly opted in to that package).

## Suggested alternatives

1. Treat "no publish date" as "always allowed" when `exclude-newer-package` is set for that package
2. Support a plain exemption list (e.g., `exclude-newer-exempt = ["my-pkg"]`) for packages that should bypass the check entirely
3. Support per-index `exclude-newer` so private indexes can be excluded from the global setting

## Workaround

Set `UV_EXCLUDE_NEWER` as a CI env var instead of in `pyproject.toml`. This works because Docker builds use `--frozen` and don't need resolution, but it means the protection isn't declarative.

[tool.uv.workspace]
members = [
  "apps/member-a",
  "apps/member-b",
]

[tool.uv]
conflicts = [
  [
    { package = "member-a" },
    { package = "member-b" },
  ],
]
```

and `member-a` and `member-b` `pyproject.toml` respectively look like

```
[project]
name = "member-a"
version = "0.1.0"
requires-python = ">=3.13"
dependencies = ["boto3>=1.42,<2"]

[build-system]
requires = ["hatchling"]
build-backend = "hatchling.build"
```

and 

```
[project]
name = "member-b"
version = "0.1.0"
requires-python = ">=3.13"
dependencies = ["boto3>=1.41,<1.42"]

[build-system]
requires = ["hatchling"]
build-backend = "hatchling.build"
```

It appears that without `[project]`, the conflicts are simply ignored completely so I end up with something like

```
uv lock --preview-features package-conflicts
  × No solution found when resolving dependencies:
  ╰─▶ Because member-a depends on boto3>=1.42,<2 and member-b depends on boto3>=1.41,<1.42, we can conclude that member-a and member-b are incompatible.
      And because your workspace requires member-a and member-b, we can conclude that your workspace's requirements are unsatisfiable.
```

When making the workspace root non virtual with something like

```
[project]
name = "root"
requires-python = ">=3.13,<3.14"
version = "1.0.0"
```

it works.

The interesting statements in the logs are

```
DEBUG Resolving despite existing lockfile due to change in conflicting groups: `Conflicts([])` vs. `Conflicts([ConflictSet { set: {ConflictItem { package: PackageName("member-a"), kind: Project }, ConflictItem { package: PackageName("member-b"), kind: Project }} }])`
...
```

### Platform

Darwin 25.4.0 arm64

### Version

uv 0.11.2 (02036a8ba 2026-03-26 aarch64-apple-darwin)

### Python version

3.13.12

result.title: UV doesn't add venv to existing dir with installed packages
result.body:
### Summary

So I'm not sure if this is the intent or not, but it's certainly annoying. result.title: `uv export --extra <root-extra>` omits packages introduced by a workspace member's conflicting extra
result.body:
### Summary

 When a workspace root's optional dependency activates a workspace member's extra (e.g. `root[cpu]` → `member[cpu]`), and the member declares a `conflicts` between its own `cpu`/`cuda` extras (to pick torch from different indices), `uv export --extra cpu` on the root does **not** include `torch` in the output.

When `uv export --extra cpu` runs, it sets the root's `cpu` extra but never the member's internal conflict-fork extra, so `member[cpu]` is never activated and `torch` is never included.

**Minimal reproduction:**

```
my-workspace/
├── pyproject.toml             # workspace root
└── packages/
    └── member/
        └── pyproject.toml     # workspace member
```

`packages/member/pyproject.toml`:
```toml
[project]
name = "member"
version = "0.1.0"
requires-python = ">=3.13"
dependencies = []

[project.optional-dependencies]
cpu  = ["torch>=2.0.0"]
cuda = ["torch>=2.0.0"]

[tool.uv]
conflicts = [
  [{ extra = "cpu" }, { extra = "cuda" }],
]

[tool.uv.sources]
torch = [
  { index = "torch-cpu",  extra = "cpu"  },
  { index = "torch-cuda", extra = "cuda" },
]

[[tool.uv.index]]
name = "torch-cpu"
url = "https://download.pytorch.org/whl/cpu"
explicit = true

[[tool.uv.index]]
name = "torch-cuda"
url = "https://download.pytorch.org/whl/cu130"
explicit = true
```

pyproject.toml (root):
```toml
[project]
name = "root"
version = "0.1.0"
requires-python = ">=3.13"
dependencies = ["member"]

[project.optional-dependencies]
cpu  = ["member[cpu]"]
cuda = ["member[cuda]"]

[tool.uv.sources]
member = { workspace = true }

[tool.uv.workspace]
members = ["packages/member"]
```

**Steps:**
```bash
uv lock
uv export --extra cpu --frozen --output-file pylock.toml
grep torch pylock.toml   # empty — torch is missing
```

**Expected:** `torch==<version>` (from the CPU index) appears in the output.

**Actual:** `torch` is absent. It only appears as a `# via` comment on other packages' entries.

### Platform

mac OS Tahoe 26.4

### Version

uv 0.11.3

### Python version

Python 3.13

Triage for astral-sh/uv#18890: "uv version 0.11.x appears to be broken for macos"

**Summary of the issue:** On an M1 MacBook Pro running macOS 15.7.4, every uv 0.11.x command panics with `Failed to build HTTP client: InvalidCertificate(UnsupportedCriticalExtension)`. uv 0.10.12 works. The reporter tested 0.11.3 and other 0.11.x releases, and the failure reproduces consistently. The reporter is behind a corporate VPN, which points to a certificate-related cause.

**Labels:**
- `bug`: a panic on a supported platform is a bug.
- `area:macos`: the report is specific to macOS.
- `area:network`: the failure is in TLS/certificate handling.

I did not suggest `needs-mre` because the report already includes a minimal reproduction.

**Duplicates:** I searched twice and found no earlier issue reporting the same panic. The two results (#5448 on a permission error and #9243 on `--native-tls`/`SSL_CERT_FILE` problems) are different problems, so I did not mark this as a duplicate.

It also asks for `RUST_BACKTRACE=1 -vvv` output. It makes no promises about fixes or timelines.

Labels: `bug`, `area:macos`, `area:network`. Not a duplicate. Next step for a maintainer is to confirm the bisect (0.10.12 good, 0.11.x bad) and check whether the native-TLS workaround avoids the panic.

result.body:
When trying to install `uv` in our CI env I noticed that Windows 2016 boxes failed to download
the install script because of `Could not create SSL/TLS secure channel`. Later Windows versions were fine.

I worked around it with:
```powershell
[Net.ServicePointManager]::SecurityProtocol = [Net.SecurityProtocolType]::Tls12;
irm https://astral.sh/uv/install.ps1 | iex
```

Perhaphs it'd be good to add it to the docs?

args.body:
Thanks for the report! The error comes from PowerShell's `irm` failing to establish a trusted SSL/TLS connection to https://astral.sh, before uv itself runs.

A few things that may help:

1. On older Windows versions, PowerShell may not negotiate TLS 1.2 by default. You can try enabling it for the current session and then re-running the installer:
   ```powershell
   [Net.ServicePointManager]::SecurityProtocol = [Net.SecurityProtocolType]::Tls12
   irm https://astral.sh/uv/install.ps1 | iex
   ```
   This is the same workaround reported in #2085.
2. Make sure Windows is up to date, since outdated root certificates can cause "trust relationship" errors.
3. If you're behind a corporate proxy or using antivirus/endpoint software that inspects HTTPS traffic, its certificate may not be trusted by this system, which can cause the same error.

Could you let us know whether the workaround above works for you? If it doesn't, the output of `$PSVersionTable` and whether you're on a proxy or network with HTTPS inspection would be helpful.

result.title: Only apply `exclude-newer` under dependency version constraints
result.body:
### Summary

The current behavior of `exclude-newer` makes it quite difficult to use in various scenarios:
* when there is version released fixing a critical issues, we need to update then manage a whitelist, see https://github.com/astral-sh/uv/issues/18792
* dependency update bots need to deal with that ? or be more coupled to the package manager
* it pollutes the lock file with timestamp information

I would instead suggest this setting to only apply when `uv` pick a version and not when setting a version range. This is happening mostly on "lock" when `uv` as to decide to pick a new transitive dependency, or pick a new version of a dependency specified with a boundary (like `>=1.0`), but only there.

So if I say they want to use 1.0.2, `uv` should just comply to that, regardless the age of 1.0.2. The same, if I specify I want to use 1.0.2 and there is a min possible version of a transitive dependency that is too young, it should still use it, because it is a choice of mine.

On the contrary, if I am running `uv lock` and I delegate to uv the role to pin specific versions, I am expecting `uv` to follow the `exclude-newer` settings

### Example

## Triage for astral-sh/uv#18914: "Only apply `exclude-newer` under dependency version constraints"

**Summary:** The reporter (vmaurin) proposes that `exclude-newer` should only filter the versions uv chooses during locking. An exact pin such as `1.0.2`, or a transitive dependency with an explicit lower bound, should be honored even if that version is newer than the cutoff. They also point out that the timestamps written to the lockfile are a pain point, and they link #18792 as an example of a critical fix being held back.

**Suggested labels** (all exist in the repo):
- `enhancement`: a change in how an existing feature behaves
- `area:lock`: the change affects universal resolution and locking
- `area:resolver`: the change affects version selection
- `needs-design`: this changes the semantics of a user-facing setting and needs discussion before anyone implements it

**Final triage:** Accept as a design/enhancement request. Apply `enhancement`, `area:lock`, `area:resolver`, and `needs-design`. Not a duplicate. Triage for astral-sh/uv#18916: "Some issues with doctests in the uv_keyring crate"

**Summary:** Packagers (Fedora) started seeing `uv-keyring` doctest failures in uv 0.11.3. The reporter reproduced them with `cargo test -p uv-keyring`. The doctests now compile and run, and three of four fail: they `use keyring::...` without that crate being available, and the `readme` example calls `.await` inside a non-async `main`.

**Suggested labels:**
- `bug`: the doctests fail under `cargo test` on the reporter's checkout.
- `area:authentication`: the crate is the keyring/credential-storage library.

I did not suggest `area:rustlib`. It might fit since this is a library crate, but the issue is about test setup, not the library API, so I left it for you to decide.

**Duplicate check:** Searches for "uv-keyring doctests fail unresolved import keyring" and "doctest failure crate" returned no earlier issues. I'm not marking this as a duplicate.

**Draft reply:** Drafted (not posted). It thanks the reporter, explains that the failing snippets reference an unavailable `keyring` crate and use `.await` in a non-async `main`, says the team will look at the doctest setup, and makes no promises about timing.

**Final triage:** Labels `bug` and `area:authentication`. New issue, not a duplicate. Reply drafted. A maintainer should check whether these doctests should be marked `ignore`/`no_run`, given the crate and the examples, or fixed so they compile.

result.title: Hyphens in index names with UV_INDEX_{name}_XXX environment variables?
result.body:
### Question

Let us say I have an index with a hyphen in its name

```
[[tool.uv.index]]
name = "my-index"
```

Then I want to set credentials using the environment variables 
`UV_INDEX_{name}_USERNAME` and `UV_INDEX_{name}_PASSWORD`

Hyphens are not allowed in variable names in a shell. You can’t do this:

`export UV_INDEX_MY-INDEX_USERNAME="..."`

The documentation only uses the simple example of `foo`, and offers no further guidance. What should be done in these cases?

### Platform

Darwin 25.3.0 arm64

### Version

uv 0.11.3 (Homebrew 2026-04-01 aarch64-apple-darwin)

Thanks for the report, and for cross-posting the link to pytorch/vision.

From the lock excerpt, the aarch64 wheels for `torchvision==0.26.0+cu128` are recorded without a `hash` field, while the x86_64 wheels have one. - The full `uv.lock` (or the relevant `torchvision` entry) and the `uv version` you used
- The exact command that fails, and whether it happens with `uv sync`, `uv lock`, or `uv pip install`
- Whether `uv lock --refresh` (or deleting the cache) changes the result

Thanks!

args.body:
Thanks for the report, and for cross-posting the link to pytorch/vision.

From the lock excerpt, the aarch64 wheels for `torchvision==0.26.0+cu128` are recorded without a `hash` field, while the x86_64 wheels have one. The error suggests that uv downloaded the aarch64 wheel, computed its hash, and compared it against the set of hashes recorded for the package. Since the aarch64 hash isn't in that set, the check fails. This may be caused by how the index publishes these files, so it may be outside uv itself, but we'd like to confirm.

- The full `uv.lock` (or the relevant `torchvision` entry) and the `uv version` you used
- The exact command that fails, and whether it happens with `uv sync`, `uv lock`, or `uv pip install`
- Whether `uv lock --refresh` (or deleting the cache) changes the result

Thanks!

- Duplicate: no.
- Next step: a maintainer should check whether the PyTorch index is serving aarch64 wheels without hashes. If it is, this is probably an upstream issue to coordinate with PyTorch. The reporter's requested details would help confirm this.

## Triage for astral-sh/uv#18940: "cant activate python venv via nu shell batch"

**Summary:** On Windows 11, running `overlay use ./.venv/Scripts/activate.nu` in nushell fails with `nu::shell::name_not_found`. The script's line `$env | get $path_name` looks up a name that nushell doesn't find, and nushell suggests `path`. This looks like a Windows and nushell case-sensitivity problem in uv's generated `activate.nu` template, not in the user's project. The reporter's `uv sync` ran fine.

**Labels to apply:**
- `bug`: the activation script fails for a supported shell.
- `area:environments`: the problem is in virtual environment activation.
- `area:windows`: the failure is specific to Windows.

I did not suggest `needs-mre`, since the report includes the error, the uv version (0.11.5), the platform, and the nushell error with its source location.

**Duplicates:** No duplicate found, so I did not mark it as one.
- #14888 ("activate.nu is incompatible with nushell 0.106.0") is closed and is about nushell version compatibility. It may be related, but I'm not confident it's the same bug, so I didn't mark it as a duplicate. A maintainer should check whether the fix for #14888 covers this Windows `PATH` lookup.
- #15294 (integration tests for venv activation scripts) is open and relevant as a place where a regression test for this could go.

**Draft reply:** I drafted a comment (not posted) that explains the likely cause, gives a workaround, and asks for the output of a command that confirms the exact variable name. Before posting, I'd tighten two things:
- "We're looking into it" reads as a commitment. Consider removing it or saying "a maintainer will take a look."
- The workaround ("setting the variables directly") is vague. Either give concrete steps or drop it.

**Final triage:** Labels `bug`, `area:environments`, `area:windows`. No duplicate. Related to closed #14888 and open #15294; a maintainer should check the Windows `PATH` lookup in the nushell template. Reply drafted and ready for review.

result.title: Should Astral learn from its own blog stop teaching bad package hygiene practices to its users?
result.body:
### Question

Astral has recently published a great article that discusses among other things supply chain security:

https://astral.sh/blog/open-source-security-at-astral

> We require all actions to be pinned to specific commits (rather than tags or branches, which are mutable). Additionally, we cross-check these commits to ensure they match an actual released repository state and are not impostor commits.
> (...)
> However, while necessary, this isn't sufficient: hash-pinning ensures that the action's contents are immutable, but doesn't prevent those immutable contents from making mutable decisions (such as installing the latest version of a binary from a GitHub repository's releases). 

But when we look at the kind of instructions you provide to the users of your own tools, two of them are as bad as `curl https://example.com/just-trust-me-bro.sh | sh` and the other has the classic "pin to `@latest`" practice.

https://github.com/astral-sh/uv?tab=readme-ov-file#installation

> Install uv with our standalone installers:
```sh
curl -LsSf https://astral.sh/uv/install.sh | sh
```

https://github.com/astral-sh/ruff?tab=readme-ov-file#installation

> Or install Ruff with uv (recommended), pip, or pipx:
```sh
uv tool install ruff@latest  # Install Ruff globally.
```

https://docs.astral.sh/ty/installation/#installing-with-the-standalone-installer

> Use curl to download the script and execute it with sh:
```
curl -LsSf https://astral.sh/ty/install.sh | sh
```

result.title: uv why  # shows why a package is included
result.body:
### Summary

First of all, thanks everyone for this amazing piece of software. You have finally made dependency management in Python as good as the language itself!

My request is to have a `uv why` command that shows why a particular package is included in the dependency tree. I maintain several packages and we typically check for vulnerabilities with `pip-audit`. When vulnerabilities show up, including fix versions, it is still quite some work to find out which (top-level) dependency called for the "culprit".

This request is based on my familiarity with [Julia's Pkg.why](https://pkgdocs.julialang.org/v1/api/#Pkg.why). I believe something like this should be fairly straightforward in uv too.

Let me know if anything is not clear or if there is any way in which I can help.

### Example

````
$ uv run pip-audit
Using CPython 3.13.3
Creating virtual environment at: .venv
      Built xyzpi @ file:///C:/gitrepos/review/xyz-kpi
Installed 50 packages in 2.53s
Found 2 known vulnerabilities in 2 packages
Name     Version ID             Fix Versions                                   
 -------- ------- -------------- ------------                                    
pygments 2.19.2  CVE-2026-4539  2.20.0                                          
requests 2.32.5  CVE-2026-25645 2.33.0                                          
Name  Skip Reason                                                               
----- ---------------------------------------------------------------------     
xyzpi Dependency not found on PyPI and could not be audited: xyzpi (2.1.18)                                                                                     /c/gitrepos/review/xyz-kpi (clean-utils-etc)
$ uv why pygments
error: unrecognized subcommand 'why'
````

This should then return which (multiple?) of the top-level packages (down the line) requires pygments.

result.title: Provide a clean “version-only” output option for uv python list
result.body:
### Summary

Currently, uv python list outputs detailed information about installed Python distributions, including full identifiers and platform-specific metadata, for example:
```
cpython-3.14.3-windows-x86_64-none  C:\Users\...\python.exe
```
While this is useful for debugging and environment inspection, it becomes noisy when the user only wants to know which Python versions are installed.

There is currently no built-in option to display only the installed Python versions in a clean and minimal format.

It would be useful to have a dedicated flag or output format that returns only version numbers (e.g. 3.11.7, 3.14.3) without implementation details, architecture strings, or file paths.

### Example

### Current behavior

```bash
uv python list --only-installed
```

Output:

```
cpython-3.14.3-windows-x86_64-none  C:\Users\...\python.exe
cpython-3.11.7-windows-x86_64-none  C:\Users\...\python.exe
```

---

### Proposed behavior

A new flag such as:

```bash
uv python list --versions-only
```

or:

```bash
uv python list --format version
```

would output:

```
3.11.7
3.14.3
```

---

### Benefit

* Cleaner CLI output for humans
* Easier parsing for scripts and automation
* Avoids the need for regex filtering or external processing
* Improves usability for version selection workflows

### Summary

On macOS 26.4 (Darwin ~25.x), uv resolves pyobjc-framework-AVFoundation to v9.2 instead of v12.1, despite the upstream package declaring a platform_release >= '22.0' condition that should select >=10.0 on this platform.

### Steps to reproduce

- pyproject.toml

```toml
[project]
name = "photos-tools"
version = "0.3.0"
requires-python = ">=3.13"
dependencies = ["osxphotos"]
```

```bash
rm -f uv.lock && rm -fr .venv
uv cache clean
uv lock
uv sync
```

### Expected behaviour

pyobjc-framework-AVFoundation>=10.0 (e.g. v12.1) is selected because platform_release on macOS 26.4 evaluates to ~25.x, which satisfies >= '22.0'.


### Actual Behaviour
uv selects pyobjc-framework-AVFoundation==9.2, triggering a transitive build failure:
```
× Failed to build `pyobjc-framework-coremedia==9.2`
  ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'pkg_resources'
```
The help: line in the uv output confirms it resolved pyobjc-framework-avfoundation v9.2 through osxphotos.


#### Full uv sync output

<summary>Click for details
<details>

```py
Resolved 83 packages in 2ms
  × Failed to build `pyobjc-framework-coremedia==9.2`
  ├─▶ The build backend returned an error
  ╰─▶ Call to `setuptools.build_meta.build_wheel` failed (exit status: 1)

      [stderr]
      Traceback (most recent call last):
        File "<string>", line 14, in <module>
          requires = get_requires_for_build({})
        File "/Users/msp/.cache/uv/builds-v0/.tmpMylmLG/lib/python3.14/site-packages/setuptools/build_meta.py", line 333, in get_requires_for_build_wheel
          return self._get_build_requires(config_settings, requirements=[])
                 ~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~~^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
        File "/Users/msp/.cache/uv/builds-v0/.tmpMylmLG/lib/python3.14/site-packages/setuptools/build_meta.py", line 301, in _get_build_requires
          self.run_setup()
          ~~~~~~~~~~~~~~^^
        File "/Users/msp/.cache/uv/builds-v0/.tmpMylmLG/lib/python3.14/site-packages/setuptools/build_meta.py", line 317, in run_setup
          exec(code, locals())
          ~~~~^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
        File "<string>", line 15, in <module>
          else:
        File "/Users/msp/.cache/uv/sdists-v9/pypi/pyobjc-framework-coremedia/9.2/m1kpMmiE4OCHmsaRyCEN2/src/pyobjc_setup.py", line 15, in <module>
          import pkg_resources
      ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'pkg_resources'

      hint: This error likely indicates that `pyobjc-framework-coremedia@9.2` depends on `pkg_resources`, but doesn't declare it as a build dependency. If
      `pyobjc-framework-coremedia` is a first-party package, consider adding `pkg_resources` to its `build-system.requires`. Otherwise, either add it to your `pyproject.toml`
      under:

      [tool.uv.extra-build-dependencies]
      pyobjc-framework-coremedia = ["pkg_resources"]

      or `uv pip install pkg_resources` into the environment and re-run with `--no-build-isolation`.
  help: `pyobjc-framework-coremedia` (v9.2) was included because `photos-tools` (v0.3.0) depends on `osxphotos` (v0.75.6) which depends on `pyobjc-framework-avfoundation` (v9.2)
        which depends on `pyobjc-framewo
```

</details>
</summary>

### Root Cause (Hypothesis)
osxphotos uses mutually exclusive platform_release markers:
```toml
pyobjc-framework-AVFoundation>=9.0,<10.0; platform_release < '22.0'
pyobjc-framework-AVFoundation>=10.0;      platform_release >= '22.0'
```
On macOS 26.4, platform_release is approximately 25.x. The string comparison '25.x' >= '22.0' is True, so the second branch should be selected.
uv appears to either:

- Be performing universal (cross-platform) resolution and taking the lowest common version across both branches, or
- Mishandling the platform_release string comparison for two-digit Darwin kernel versions (e.g. 25.x vs 22.x)

### Workaround
Adding an explicit override resolves the issue:
```toml
[tool.uv]
override-dependencies = [
    "pyobjc-framework-avfoundation>=12.0",
]
```
### Additional Context

Python 3.
[truncated]

Triage for astral-sh/uv#18971: "platform_release marker misresolved on macOS 26 — picks wrong version branch of conditional dependency"

**Labels to apply**
- `bug`: the resolver selects the wrong branch of a conditional dependency, and the lock then fails to build.
- `area:resolver`: the problem is in how markers are evaluated during resolution.
- `area:macos`: the report is specific to macOS.
- `area:lock`: the resolution is a universal lock, and the reporter suspects universal resolution is combining the two branches.

I didn't add `needs-mre`. The report includes a minimal pyproject.toml and exact commands, so it's reproducible on macOS.

**Duplicates**
Searches for "platform_release marker macOS resolution pyobjc" and "pkg_resources build failure pyobjc-framework" returned no similar earlier issues, so I haven't marked it as a duplicate.

I drafted a comment asking for `uv --version`, `uv lock -v` output, the local `platform.release()` value, and the relevant `uv.lock` entries for `pyobjc-framework-avfoundation`. It's saved as a draft only; nothing has been posted.

**Notes**
- The issue body returned to me was truncated at "Python 3.", so I couldn't see the rest of the environment details. The draft asks for the uv version, which may already be in the missing part.
- The reporter's root-cause hypothesis is plausible, but I haven't verified it. The workaround (`override-dependencies`) suggests the marker branches are being combined rather than evaluated per platform. A maintainer should check whether the `platform_release` comparison is the problem or whether universal resolution is at fault.

result.title: Custom pip index with project with a period in the name causing issues.
result.body:
### Summary

Hello,

I currently host a [custom pip index](https://about.abstractumbra.dev/pip/) for a community I'm  a part of. The project name in question is `discord.py` and currently it's causing some issues with installing the project.

I recently had to correct how the CI built and contained the wheels for each directory due to [a comment on discourse](https://discuss.python.org/t/what-would-it-look-like-to-deprecate-pep-503/106959/19).
I now normalise the names through [`packaging.utils.parse_wheel_filename`](https://packaging.pypa.io/en/stable/utils.html#packaging.utils.parse_wheel_filename) to correctly get the distribution name (so `discord-py` in this case).
However the built wheel for `discord.py` is named `discord_py` (an `_` instead of a `.`) and this is accepted by the packaging tooling.

When attempting to install/add with `uv` the following occurs:

<details>
<summary>uv add</summary>

```sh
❯ uv add discord.py --index-url https://abstractumbra.github.io/pip
warning: Indexes specified via `--index-url` will not be persisted to the `pyproject.toml` file; use `--default-index` instead.
⠹ brotli==1.2.0                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                            error: Failed to fetch: `https://abstractumbra.github.io/pip/discord-py/discord.py-2.7.1-py3-none-any.whl`
  Caused by: HTTP status client error (404 Not Found) for url (https://about.abstractumbra.dev/pip/discord-py/discord.py-2.7.1-py3-none-any.whl)
```

</details>
(the `--index-url` is purely for testing, it's designed as an extra index url not a primary).

I suspect the issue is that `uv` is not aware of, or respecting the """correct""" normalised names of projects with a period in the name, as `pip` works just fine:

<details>
<summary>pip install</summary>

```sh
❯ pip install --index-url https://abstractumbra.github.io/pip discord.py

     - 85.8 kB ? 0:00:00
