result.title: uv git dependency fetch breaks when GIT_DIR is set in environment
result.body:
### Summary

When running a script via `uv run` that depends on a Git dependency, uv’s internal git fetch may misbehave if the environment variable `GIT_DIR` is set. This can easily happen with `git bisect run uv run`.

For me, this had the effect of breaking the `uv run`:
```
   Updating https://github.com/labgrid-project/labgrid (master)
  × Failed to download and build `labgrid @ git+https://github.com/labgrid-project/labgrid@master`
  ├─▶ Git operation failed
  ├─▶ failed to clone into: /home/afa/.cache/uv/git-v0/db/97a5d45ad0e4ae1c
  ├─▶ failed to fetch commit `c246fab86fe451db46507b77bc7fe58aaad3a79e`
  ╰─▶ process didn't exit successfully: `/usr/lib/git-core/git fetch --force --update-head-ok 'https://github.com/labgrid-project/labgrid'
      '+c246fab86fe451db46507b77bc7fe58aaad3a79e:refs/commit/c246fab86fe451db46507b77bc7fe58aaad3a79e'` (exit status: 128)
      --- stderr
      fatal: not a git repository (or any parent up to mount point /home)
      Stopping at filesystem boundary (GIT_DISCOVERY_ACROSS_FILESYSTEM not set).
```

and mangling the repository I wanted to bisect:

```
fatal: this operation must be run in a work tree
```

Because `uv` turned it into a bare directory, instead of presumably `~/cache/uv/git-v0` instead.
I turned it back to a regular repository with:
```
git config set core.bare false
```

But I am not sure yet, what other unintended modifications `uv` may have done to my git repository.

I reproduced with uv 0.7.13 and git version 2.47.3.

This is similar to https://github.com/astral-sh/uv/issues/16102 which was closed after a workaround was found.

Due to the potential for data loss, I think `uv` should explicitly unset `GIT_DIR` and possibly other variables that can influence what repo `uv`'s internal git invocations operate on.

### Platform

Linux 6.19.6+deb13-amd64 x86_64 GNU/Linux

### Version

uv 0.7.13

### Python version

Python 3.13.5

result.title: uv constantly warns about empty `SSL_CERT_DIR`
result.body:
### Summary

With the 0.11.X release of uv, there are constant warnings about an empty `SSL_CERT_DIR`.

Reproduce with conda:
1. conda create -n uv_bug python=3.14 -y
2. conda activate uv_bug
3. pip install "uv>=0.11"
4. uv pip install numpy

This will yield: `warning: Ignoring `SSL_CERT_DIR`. No certificates found in:` which will also show up with other uv commands.

The problem is that conda by default creates an activation script for openssl in the environment (e.g., in `%userprofile%\miniforge3\envs\pref\etc\conda\activate.d`) with the following content:
```powershell
if (-not $Env:SSL_CERT_FILE) {
    $Env:SSL_CERT_FILE = "$Env:CONDA_PREFIX\Library\ssl\cacert.pem"
    $Env:__CONDA_OPENSSL_CERT_FILE_SET = "1"
}
if (-not $Env:SSL_CERT_DIR) {
    $Env:SSL_CERT_DIR = "$Env:CONDA_PREFIX\Library\ssl\certs"
    $Env:__CONDA_OPENSSL_CERT_DIR_SET = "1"
}
```

By default, `$Env:CONDA_PREFIX\Library\ssl\cacert.pem` points to an existing file but `$Env:CONDA_PREFIX\Library\ssl\certs` is empty (strictly speaking it only contains a `.keep` file). The latter is causing the warning message. One could argue that conda should not point `SSL_CERT_DIR` to an empty directory but I also think that uv should not warn about this if `SSL_CERT_FILE` points already to an existing file.

uv 0.10.X did not have this warning. Unfortunately, this warning is emitted with every uv command.

Windows 11

### Version

0.11.6

### Python version

3.14.4

**Issue:** "uv constantly warns about empty `SSL_CERT_DIR`" (uv 0.11.6, Windows 11, conda environment)

No certificates found in:` on every command. The reporter says 0.10.x did not show this warning, so it looks like a regression in 0.11.x.

**Draft reply:** Drafted with `draft_comment`, not posted. **Final triage:** Accept as a bug, label as above, no duplicate, reply drafted for maintainer review.

result.title: Provide a supported way to force uv to use only interpreters from a specific path
result.body:
### Summary

Our company has a set of managed Python interpreters. We don't want our employees to use other interpreters - including both the python-build-standalone ones and the ones that ship with the distro or OS.

With `UV_PYTHON_DOWNLOADS='never'` and `UV_PYTHON_PREFERENCE='only-system'` we can force `uv` (or a wrapper around `uv` that we provide, more likely) to never use the python-build-standalone interpreters and to only use interpreters that are already on the machine, but we don't have any reasonable way to prevent it from picking up interpreters in `/usr/bin` that come with the distro. We can't just remove `/usr/bin` from `$PATH` without breaking other things.

There's an environment variable, `UV_TEST_PYTHON_PATH`, that can be used to do exactly what we want - control the path to be used by `uv` for discovery of system interpreters without affecting the path used for other things. That exists because the `uv` test suite has the same need as we do, wanting to ignore some interpreters and only use ones found in a particular set of places.

Can that environment variable be documented as part of `uv`'s official support surface?

**Summary:** The reporter's company wants employees to use only its managed Python interpreters. `UV_PYTHON_DOWNLOADS=never` and `UV_PYTHON_PREFERENCE=only-system` stop uv from downloading its own interpreters, but uv still finds distro interpreters in `/usr/bin`. Removing `/usr/bin` from `PATH` would break other things. The reporter asks whether the undocumented `UV_TEST_PYTHON_PATH` variable, which the test suite uses to limit discovery, can be documented as supported.

**Labels (suggested, all exist in the repo):**
- `enhancement`: a new supported capability is being requested.
- `area:uv-python`: the issue concerns interpreter discovery.
- `needs-decision`: maintainers must decide whether to support `UV_TEST_PYTHON_PATH` publicly or add a different mechanism.

**Duplicate check:** No duplicate found. Searches for `UV_TEST_PYTHON_PATH`, path-restricted discovery, and managed-only interpreters turned up nothing relevant. The one hit (#4376, a Gentoo test failure in `toolchain_find.rs`) is unrelated, so I did not mark this as a duplicate.

**Draft reply:** Written with `draft_comment` and not posted. It thanks the reporter, says the request has been noted for maintainer review, and makes no promises about fixes or timelines.

**Notes for maintainers:**
- The request is less about a bug and more about whether an internal test variable should become a supported public interface. That is a design decision, which is why I suggested `needs-decision`.
- The variable is only mentioned in the issue, so I have not verified its current behavior in the codebase.

result.title: Warning when Python version is specified with `.python-version`
result.body:
### Question

uv [supports](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/concepts/python-versions/#python-version-files) `.python-version` files, which I prefer over `project.requires-python` in pyproject.toml (because the latter forces me to also set `project.name` and `project.version`).

But you get a warning every time you use `uv run` or `uv sync`:

```
warning: No `requires-python` value found in the workspace. Defaulting to `>=3.14`.
```

Considering https://github.com/astral-sh/uv/issues/8247#issuecomment-2416680597:

> The `.python-version` file is not quite obsolete with `requires-python` -- they're subtly different. `requires-python` is the range of versions supported by your project. `.python-version` is the exact version you want to use when developing. For example, if you're working on a library, your `requires-python` might be `>= "3.10"`. But when developing on your machine, you might want to use `3.12.4` by default -- so you'd set that in a `.python-version`.

The warning seems a bit too aggressive. It might make more sense to warn only if no Python version was requested at all?

### Platform

macOS Sequoia 15.7.5

### Version

uv 0.11.7 (Homebrew 2026-04-15 x86_64-apple-darwin)

result.title: `uv add --bounds=major` puts upper bound on minor version for 0.y.z packages
result.body:
### Summary

```fish
uv add --bounds=major whenever
```

```pip-requirements
whenever>=0.10.0,<0.11.0
```

and

```fish
uv add --bounds=minor whenever
```

```pip-requirements
whenever>=0.10.0,<0.10.1
```

For a major version zero package, `--bounds=major` sets an upper bound on the _minor_ version, and `--bounds=minor` sets an upper bound on the patch version (which, for 0.y.z versioning, effectively pins an exact version).

### Platform

macOS Sequoia 15.7.5

### Version

uv 0.11.7 (Homebrew 2026-04-15 x86_64-apple-darwin)

result.title: URL Dependency Issue in Workspace Packages with Build Dependencies on Other Workspace Packages
result.body:
### Summary

In a project that only uses workspace packages, I get this error when building a workspace package which has a build-dependency on another workspace package which has a dependency on another workspace package. In my example, `my-tool` lists `my-backend` as a build-dependency. `my-backend` depends on `my-util`.

```
$ uv build --wheel --package my-tool
Building wheel...
  × Failed to build `/home/user/uv-testing/my-workspace/my-tool`
  ├─▶ Failed to resolve requirements from `build-system.requires`
  ├─▶ No solution found when resolving: `my-backend @ file:///home/user/uv-testing/my-workspace/my-backend`
  ├─▶ Failed to resolve dependencies for package `my-backend==0.1.0`
  ╰─▶ Package `my-util` was included as a URL dependency. URL dependencies must be expressed as direct requirements or
      constraints. Consider adding `my-util @ file:///home/user/uv-testing/my-workspace/my-util` to your dependencies
      or constraints file.
```

I cannot tell whether this is a bug or something that is covered by https://docs.astral.sh/uv/reference/internals/resolver/#url-dependencies. To me, it seems as though depending on workspace packages doesn't count as an "index package" and isn't subject to the same issues that resolving index packages have (since we directly list `workspace = true` as the source of the package). Since neither `my-util` nor `my-backend` is included as a dependency in `my-tool`'s wheel, it seems wrong to enforce these resolution requirements onto building.

The docs state, 

> uv requires that URLs are either declared directly ... or by other URL dependencies.

In the error it seems as though my-backend is attempting to be resolved as a URL dependency (I guess something happens in uv which takes a workspace package and transforms it to a URL dependency) and hence it should be OK for it to include other url dependencies.

### Reproducible Pyprojects

The pyproject's for the example are as follows:

**my-workspace/pyproject.toml**
```toml
[project]
name = "my-workspace"
version = "0.1.0"
description = "Add your description here"
readme = "README.md"
requires-python = ">=3.12"
dependencies = []

[tool.uv]
package = false

[tool.uv.workspace]
members = ["my-util", "my-backend", "my-tool"]

[tool.uv.sources]
my-backend = { workspace = true }
my-util = { workspace = true }
```

**my-workspace/my-util/pyproject.toml**
```toml
[project]
name = "my-util"
version = "0.1.0"
description = "Add your description here"
readme = "README.md"
requires-python = ">=3.12"
dependencies = []
```

**my-workspace/my-backend/pyproject.toml**
```toml
[project]
name = "my-backend"
version = "0.1.0"
description = "Add your description here"
readme = "README.md"
requires-python = ">=3.12"
dependencies = ["my-util"]
```

**my-workspace/my-tool/pyproject.toml**
```toml
[project]
name = "my-tool"
version = "0.1.0"
description = "Add your description here"
readme = "README.md"
requires-python = ">=3.12"
dependencies = []

[build-system]
requires = ["my-backend", "setuptools"] # note setuptools is included here since I didn't actually make a real backend for this example, but it should be irrelevant to this issue
```

### Workarounds

The most succinct workaround is to have `my-tool` declare `my-util` as a build-dependency. I.e.

**my-workspace/my-tool/pyproject.toml**
```toml
[project]
name = "my-tool"
version = "0.1.0"
description = "Add your description here"
readme = "README.md"
requires-python = ">=3.12"
dependencies = []

[build-system]
requires = ["my-backend", "setuptools", "my-util"] 
```

In my circumstance, I have a really large workspace with 100s of workspace packages which all depend on `my-backend` or equivalent sort of packages (i.e. plugins). These plugins can be changed often and their dependencies on other local workspace packages can also be changed. It is a pain to go through every dependent workspace package to update their build dependencies with the new transitive dependencies that are necessary for the build plu

## Triage for astral-sh/uv #19074

**Summary:** Building `my-tool` fails when its `build-system.requires` lists `my-backend`, a workspace package that depends on another workspace package, `my-util`. uv reports `my-util` as a URL dependency that isn't declared directly. The reporter asks whether this is a bug or documented behavior. The report includes a complete reproduction and a workaround.

**Suggested labels (all exist in the repo):**
- `bug`: the reporter's expectation looks reasonable, since workspace members are resolved from local paths and not from an index, but the maintainers still need to confirm this.
- `area:workspaces`: the failure involves workspace members and their sources.
- `area:sources`: the error concerns how path/URL-style dependencies are resolved transitively.

I didn't add `question` or `needs-mre` because the report is a bug candidate with a full reproduction.

**Duplicate check:** No duplicate found. The closest matches were:
- #11760, "Dependency resolution failure on transitive Git build-system requirement" (open). It is the same class of failure, a transitive URL-style build requirement, but it involves Git sources, not workspace path sources. I didn't mark it as a duplicate, but it's worth linking as related and checking whether a fix for one would cover the other.
- #16066, "How to enforce runtime version consistency for project build requirements?" (open). Only loosely related.

**Draft reply:** I drafted a short, neutral comment. It acknowledges the reproduction, notes the link to the resolver's URL dependency rules, says it isn't yet clear whether this is intended, and mentions the workaround. It makes no promises about fixes or timelines. My first draft said the maintainers had "looked at it" and would "follow up," which wasn't accurate, so I replaced it. The draft has not been posted.

**Next steps for maintainers:**
1. Decide whether workspace members resolved as URL dependencies should be allowed to carry their own transitive URL dependencies. The docs' current rule suggests they aren't.
2. If the answer is "bug," link #11760 and check whether the same fix applies.
3. Consider whether the docs should call out this build-system case explicitly.

result.title: No-op timestamp for `exclude-newer-package` with spans
result.body:
### Summary

I just discovered #19022 while subscribed to #18708, and it looks like a great improvement to eliminate timestamp noise.

In the same spirit of this workaround, I just wonder if we could use the sane no-op flag for `[options.exclude-newer-package]`.

See how a package configured with a relative span (like `0 day`), the lockfile records the a full timestamp:

```toml
[options]
exclude-newer = "0001-01-01T00:00:00Z" # no-op placeholder (fixed by #19022)
exclude-newer-span = "P1W"

[options.exclude-newer-package]
mypackage = { timestamp = "2026-04-21T14:32:07.819274Z", span = "PT0S" }  # still changes every run
```

So currently every `uv lock` invokation update the `timestamp`.

### Example

Configuration in `pyproject.toml`:

```toml
[tool.uv]
exclude-newer = "1 week"
exclude-newer-package = { mypackage = "0 day" }
```

Running `uv lock` twice in quick succession produces a diff:

```diff
 [options.exclude-newer-package]
-mypackage = { timestamp = "2026-04-21T14:32:07.819274Z", span = "PT0S" }
+mypackage = { timestamp = "2026-04-21T14:32:09.123456Z", span = "PT0S" }
```

My proposal is to reuse the same no-op placeholder when a span is present:

```toml
[options.exclude-newer-package]
mypackage = { timestamp = "0001-01-01T00:00:00Z", span = "PT0S" }
```

This would make the lockfile fully stable across runs.

result.title: uv python pin does not successfully pin you to a patch version
result.body:
### Summary

If you use `uv python pin 3.x.y` to pin to the latest patch version installed on the system, `uv sync` wrongly creates a venv pointing at the mutable 3.x symlink, not at 3.x.y directly, meaning that an unrelated action triggering a download of a newer 3.x.z will cause the venv to do a transparent upgrade to 3.x.z, contrary to the pin.

```
$ uv self version
uv 0.11.7 (x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu)
$ uv python list '>=3.14.3,<3.15-gnu'
cpython-3.14.4-linux-x86_64-gnu    <download available>
cpython-3.14.3-linux-x86_64-gnu    .local/share/uv/python/cpython-3.14-linux-x86_64-gnu/bin/python3.14
$ uv init pinme
Initialized project `pinme` at `/home/ubuntu/pinme`
$ cd pinme
$ uv python pin 3.14.3
Updated `.python-version` from `3.14` -> `3.14.3`
$ uv sync
Using CPython 3.14.3
Creating virtual environment at: .venv
Resolved 1 package in 2ms
Checked in 0.00ms
$ .venv/bin/python -V
Python 3.14.3
$ uvx python3.14.4 -c True
[triggers a download]
$ .venv/bin/python -V
Python 3.14.4
$ readlink .venv/bin/python
/home/ubuntu/.local/share/uv/python/cpython-3.14-linux-x86_64-gnu/bin/python3.14
$ head -n1 .venv/pyvenv.cfg 
home = /home/ubuntu/.local/share/uv/python/cpython-3.14-linux-x86_64-gnu/bin
```

Interestingly, uv _now_ realizes that the venv is incorrect and recreates it (hence using .venv/bin/python directly above):

```
$ uv run python -V
Using CPython 3.14.3
Removed virtual environment at: .venv
Creating virtual environment at: .venv
Python 3.14.3
$ readlink .venv/bin/python
/home/ubuntu/.local/share/uv/python/cpython-3.14.3-linux-x86_64-gnu/bin/python3.14
$ head -n1 .venv/pyvenv.cfg 
home = /home/ubuntu/.local/share/uv/python/cpython-3.14.3-linux-x86_64-gnu/bin
```

I believe this is a regression between 0.11.6 and 0.11.7, almost certainly surfaced by 9aee91cf00ff03f23f89e0353e53be3131ce11a1 (though the bug is probably somewhere else), cc @zanieb.

### Platform

Linux, but also reproduces on Windows

### Version

0.11.7

### Python version

_No response_

result.title: `[dependency-groups]` entry `pkg[extra]` stops activating `extra` once `[tool.uv.conflicts]` lists it
result.body:
### Summary

When `[dependency-groups]` contains an entry that references a self-extra (`pkg[foo]`), and that same extra is listed in `[tool.uv.conflicts]`, activating the dependency group no longer activates the extra. This makes `uv sync` (which activates default groups) and `uv sync --extra foo` diverge, even though the group is defined as `foo = ["pkg[foo]"]`.

When a `[dependency-groups]` entry references a self-extra (`pkg[foo]`) and that extra is listed in `[tool.uv.conflicts]`, `uv sync` no longer activates the extra through the default-group path. `uv sync --extra foo` works correctly, but bare `uv sync` silently drops the extra's entire dependency subtree (even though the group is defined as `foo = ["pkg[foo]"]` and is normally equivalent to `--extra foo`).
  
```toml
[dependency-groups]
dev = ["demo[dev]"]

[project]
name = "demo"
version = "0"
requires-python = ">=3.12"
dependencies = []

[project.optional-dependencies]
train = ["skyrl[skyrl-train]"]
summarize = ["vllm"]
dev = ["demo[train]"]

[tool.uv]
conflicts = [
  [{extra = "dev"}, {extra = "summarize"}],
  [{extra = "summarize"}, {extra = "train"}]
]

[tool.uv.sources]
skyrl = {git = "https://github.com/NovaSky-AI/SkyRL.git"}
```

Here's CLI usage showing the bug:

```console
$ uv lock
Resolved 230 packages in 1.13s

$ rm -rf .venv && uv sync --frozen
Using CPython 3.13.2
Creating virtual environment at: .venv
Checked in 0.00ms
# 0 packages installed

$ rm -rf .venv && uv sync --frozen --extra dev
# 112 packages installed, including skyrl, skyrl-gym, accelerate, tensordict, wandb, torchdata, ...
```

`uv.lock` contains:

```toml
[package.dev-dependencies]
dev = [
    { name = "demo" },
    { name = "demo", extra = ["dev"], marker = "extra == 'extra-4-demo-dev' or (extra == 'extra-4-demo-summarize' and extra == 'extra-4-demo-train')" },
]
```

The `demo[dev]` reference is gated behind the synthetic conflict-group key `extra == 'extra-4-demo-dev'`. Activating the `dev` dependency group does not set this key (only `--extra dev` does), so the extra's contents (`demo[train]` → `skyrl[skyrl-train]` → 112 transitive packages) are filtered out during sync.

I expect `uv sync` and `uv sync --extra dev` to produce identical environments, since `[dependency-groups] dev = ["demo[dev]"]` is defined as "install `demo` with its `dev` extra." Notably, without `[tool.uv.conflicts]`, the two invocations are identical; adding `conflicts` silently breaks the equivalence.

Here's some issues with a possibly related underlying mechanism:

- https://github.com/astral-sh/uv/issues/13073
- https://github.com/astral-sh/uv/issues/13070

### Platform

Darwin 25.3.0 arm64

### Version

uv 0.11.7 (9d177269e 2026-04-15 aarch64-apple-darwin)

### Python version

Python 3.13.2

result.title: uv pip uninstall removes whole site-packages directory when removing empty package with .egg-info metadata
result.body:
### Summary

When a python package is installed with `.egg-info` metadata and contains no files (`top-level.txt` is empty), `uv pip uninstall` removes the whole `site-packages` directory.

I've reproduced this also with uv 0.9.30 and 0.11.7

I have a miminal reproducer here https://github.com/ilia-eiq/uv-pip-uninstall-reproducer
Python 3.11 is required to run it, as you need older pip to have metadata installed as an egg.

Looks like the cause of the problem is that for an empty package `top-level.txt` is not actually empty, but contains one char, newline. So this code https://github.com/astral-sh/uv/blob/45b930fdc793302f675009a7f9858a148e478841/crates/uv-install-wheel/src/uninstall.rs#L244-L257 reads it as one empty string, which is when joined with dist-location https://github.com/astral-sh/uv/blob/45b930fdc793302f675009a7f9858a148e478841/crates/uv-install-wheel/src/uninstall.rs#L261 and then the whole dist-location directory is removed https://github.com/astral-sh/uv/blob/45b930fdc793302f675009a7f9858a148e478841/crates/uv-install-wheel/src/uninstall.rs#L268

### Platform

Linux

### Version

uv 0.11.6 (x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu)

result.title: Unable to use `uv self update` on armv7 host after 0.11.0
result.body:
### Summary

After 0.11.0, attempting to upgrade `uv` via `uv self update` on a 32-bit ARM host fails with:

```
$ uv self update
info: Checking for updates...
error: Failed to resolve the latest uv version
  Caused by: No version of uv found for platform `armv7-unknown-linux-gnueabihfeabihf`
```

This is reproducible on an `aarch64` host that can run 32-bit code in a fresh Debian Trixie container.

```
$ podman run --arch arm -it --rm docker.io/debian:trixie-slim /bin/sh -c 'set -x &&
	dpkg --print-architecture &&
	apt-get update >/dev/null &&
	apt-get upgrade -y >/dev/null &&
	apt-get install -y curl >/dev/null &&
	curl -LsSf https://astral.sh/uv/0.10.12/install.sh | sh &&
	. $HOME/.local/bin/env &&
	uv --version &&
	uv self update &&
	uv --version &&
	uv self update'
+ dpkg --print-architecture
armhf
+ apt-get update
+ apt-get upgrade -y
+ apt-get install -y curl
...
+ curl -LsSf https://astral.sh/uv/0.10.12/install.sh
+ sh
downloading uv 0.10.12 armv7-unknown-linux-gnueabihf
no checksums to verify
installing to /root/.local/bin
  uv
  uvx
everything's installed!

To add $HOME/.local/bin to your PATH, either restart your shell or run:

    source $HOME/.local/bin/env (sh, bash, zsh)
    source $HOME/.local/bin/env.fish (fish)
+ . /root/.local/bin/env
+ export PATH=/root/.local/bin:/usr/local/sbin:/usr/local/bin:/usr/sbin:/usr/bin:/sbin:/bin
+ uv --version
uv 0.10.12 (armv7-unknown-linux-gnueabihf)
+ uv self update
info: Checking for updates...
success: Upgraded uv from v0.10.12 to v0.11.7! https://github.com/astral-sh/uv/releases/tag/0.11.7
+ uv --version
uv 0.11.7 (armv7-unknown-linux-gnueabihf)
+ uv self update
info: Checking for updates...
error: Failed to resolve the latest uv version
  Caused by: No version of uv found for platform `armv7-unknown-linux-gnueabihfeabihf`
```

### Platform

Linux 6.12.74+deb13+1-armmp-lpae armv7l GNU/Linux

### Version

uv 0.11.7 (armv7-unknown-linux-gnueabihf)

### Python version

Python 3.14.4

[[index]]
name = "foo"

I'm not sure if I have the syntax wrong or if this is not a feature.

Windows 11

uv 0.11.7 (9d177269e 2026-04-15 x86_64-pc-windows-msvc)

result.title: Feature Request: Support querying dependencies of uninstalled packages
result.body:
### Summary

## Feature Request

It would be very useful if `uv` could provide a way to query the dependencies of a Python package without installing it. This would allow users to inspect dependency trees for packages before deciding to install them, similar to what `pipgrip` offers.

### Use Case
- Developers want to check all dependencies of a package without affecting their current environment.
- Useful for generating dependency reports or requirements files for CI/CD pipelines.

### Suggested Approach
- Integrate a feature that fetches package metadata from PyPI and parses `Requires-Dist`.
- Optionally, support recursive resolution of sub-dependencies.

Thank you for considering this feature!

## 功能请求

希望 `uv` 可以提供一个功能，用于查询 Python 包的依赖关系，而无需先安装该包。这样用户可以在决定安装前查看依赖树，类似于 `pipgrip` 的功能。

### 使用场景
- 开发者希望在不影响当前环境的情况下，查看某个包的所有依赖。
- 对于生成依赖报告或 CI/CD 流程中的 requirements 文件非常有用。

### 建议实现方式
- 增加一个功能，从 PyPI 获取包的元数据并解析 `Requires-Dist`。
- 可选：支持递归解析子依赖。

感谢考虑添加这个功能！

result.title: `uv lock` with transitive poetry path depedencies results in machine-specific path in lockfile
result.body:
### Summary

I've run into a problem trying to lock a dependency which itself uses poetry and declares relative path dependencies. The package in question is a custom fork of `DeepfilterNet` here:  https://github.com/benniekiss/DeepFilterNet

The package has a dependency on `deepfilterlib` via the relative path [declared here](https://github.com/benniekiss/DeepFilterNet/blob/d375b2d8309e0935d165700c91da9de862a99c31/DeepFilterNet/pyproject.toml#L26). I implemented this change to make building `DeepfilterNet` standalone simpler for my dev setup, but this has resulted in issues with lock file generation.

Because of the path dependency, when the lockfile is generated, the `deepfilterlib` lock is something like this:

```
	[[package]]
	name = "deepfilterlib"
	version = "0.5.7"
	source = { directory = "/Users/benniekiss/.cache/uv/git-v0/checkouts/e42607f483442963/ba2260b/pyDF" }
```

This results in sync failures when trying to install on a different machine.

Is there a way to avoid this conflict without changing the packages dependencies, or is this expected behavior?

Here is a short MRE:

```shell
mkdir -p test_lock
cd test_lock

cat <<EOF > pyproject.toml
[project]
name = "test_lock"
version = "1"
requires-python = ">=3.13,<3.14"
dependencies = [
    "deepfilternet",
]
[tool.uv.sources]
deepfilternet = [
    { git = "https://github.com/benniekiss/DeepFilterNet", subdirectory = "DeepFilterNet", branch = "dev" },
]
EOF

echo "LOCKING"
uv lock --no-cache

echo "SYNCING"
uv sync
```

### Platform

macOS 26

### Version

0.11.7

### Python version

3.13

result.title: Activate script does not work in PowerShell with UNC paths
result.body:
### Summary

This line: https://github.com/astral-sh/uv/blob/3e9c33358554168e6662007bdf533f9b9c1b40ac/crates/uv-virtualenv/src/activator/activate.ps1#L23

`$script:BASE_DIR = Split-Path (Resolve-Path "$THIS_PATH/..") -Parent`

should be replaced by:

`$script:BASE_DIR = Split-Path -Parent (Split-Path -Parent (Resolve-Path -LiteralPath $THIS_PATH))`

Why:
- Resolve-Path does not reliably normalize .. when it’s embedded in a string, especially with UNC paths (\\server\share\...)
- Using / path concatenation is also brittle on Windows

Without this correction, getting this error message:

> error: Failed to inspect Python interpreter from active virtual environment at `Microsoft.PowerShell.Core\FileSystem::\\.....\.venv\Scripts\activate.ps1\Scripts\python.exe`

### Platform

Windows 11

### Version

uv 0.11.6 (65950801c 2026-04-09 x86_64-pc-windows-msvc)

### Python version

Python 3.12.5

result.title: Is there a way to add local packages from `requirements.txt` without any pyproject.toml file present?
result.body:
### Question

I'm in the process of writing a Dockerfile. I have a Python monorepo, where some of which packages depend on local packages. I don't want the source code in the container, I only want the venv ready for the application to be cloned at runtime. At the moment I deal with this by copying every pyrpoject.toml and uv.lock in the repo, but it is not an elegant solution (I do this by ignoring everything in the .dockerignore file EXCEPT pyproject.toml and uv.lock).

I thought I could get away with using a requirements.txt file: my idea is to create this file in the CI/CD pipeline, and simply `uv add -r requirements.txt` inside the container. The problem is that uv complains that local dependencies are not present. 

I could pass `--no-emit-local` to `uv export`, but now I don't have these local packages in my `PYTHONPATH`, meaning that when I clone the repo, these packages are not found.

Lastly, I could simply use uv at runtime to add local packages, but my goal is not to have uv in the final image.

Ideally, uv would let me simply note that some local package lives in a certain folder, such that it is found by python after cloning the repo at runtime. Given I'm exporting all dependencies using `uv export` during CI/CD, I can already pre-install all dependencies of local packages even without them being present in the docker container.

Is there a solution? Am I missing something?


### Platform

Darwin 25.4.0 arm64

### Version

uv 0.11.7 (9d177269e 2026-04-15 aarch64-apple-darwin)

triage.draft_reply:
Thanks for the question! A few things that may help:

- **Link mode:** uv uses hardlinks by default, which avoids duplicating package files in each venv. If the cache and project are on different drives, hardlinks aren't possible and uv falls back to copying, which can explain the large venvs. Setting `UV_CACHE_DIR` to a location on the same drive as your projects may help (see #15878 for related discussion). You can also set `UV_LINK_MODE` explicitly to check what you're getting.
- **Re-downloads of PyTorch:** If `uv sync` keeps fetching the full wheel, it would be useful to see the output of `uv sync -v` (or `--verbose`) for one of the slow runs, along with your `pyproject.toml`/index configuration for PyTorch. A similar report about PyTorch re-downloading despite a lockfile was filed earlier in #15425, so the details will help us see whether this is the same behavior.

Thanks again for helping us improve uv!

args.body:
Thanks for the question! A few things that may help:

- **Link mode:** uv uses hardlinks by default, which avoids duplicating package files in each venv. If the cache and project are on different drives, hardlinks aren't possible and uv falls back to copying, which can explain the large venvs. Setting `UV_CACHE_DIR` to a location on the same drive as your projects may help (see #15878 for related discussion). You can also set `UV_LINK_MODE` explicitly to check what you're getting.
- **Re-downloads of PyTorch:** If `uv sync` keeps fetching the full wheel, it would be useful to see the output of `uv sync -v` (or `--verbose`) for one of the slow runs, along with your `pyproject.toml`/index configuration for PyTorch. A similar report about PyTorch re-downloading despite a lockfile was filed earlier in #15425, so the details will help us see whether this is the same behavior.

Thanks again for helping us improve uv!

result.title: `uv lock --exclude-newer-package` only reports the first changed package in the lockfile-invalidation message
result.body:
### Summary

When more than one `--exclude-newer-package` constraint changes between consecutive `uv lock` runs, the "Resolving despite existing lockfile due to …" message only reports the **first** detected change and silently drops the rest. 

### Steps to reproduce

```console
aditya@aditya:/tmp/uv-exclude-newer-package$ uv init --no-readme --bare
Initialized project `uv-exclude-newer-package`
aditya@aditya:/tmp/uv-exclude-newer-package$ uv add requests
Using CPython 3.14.2
Creating virtual environment at: .venv
Resolved 6 packages in 3ms
Installed 5 packages in 18ms
 + certifi==2026.4.22
 + charset-normalizer==3.4.7
 + idna==3.13
 + requests==2.33.1
 + urllib3==2.6.3
aditya@aditya:/tmp/uv-exclude-newer-package$ uv lock --exclude-newer-package requests=2030-01-01 --exclude-newer-package urllib3=2030-01-01
Resolving despite existing lockfile due to addition of exclude newer `2030-01-01T18:30:00Z` for package `urllib3`
Resolved 6 packages in 3ms
aditya@aditya:/tmp/uv-exclude-newer-package$ uv lock
Resolving despite existing lockfile due to removal of exclude newer for package `urllib3`
Resolved 6 packages in 5ms
```

Lockfile correctly persists both but only `urllib3` is mentioned in the logs.

### Platform

Ubuntu 24.04.2 LTS x86_64 (Linux 6.17.0-22-generic)

### Version

uv 0.11.8 (502d42bf1 2026-04-28)

### Python version

Python 3.14.2

result.title: `uv tool uninstall` silently aborts after first missing tool receipt when uninstalling multiple
result.body:
### Summary

When `uv tool uninstall` is called with multi pkg names and the first tool has a missing/corrupt receipt (such as dangling install), uv removes that tool's environment and then **returns early**, skipping other remaining names. The user sees a "Removed dangling environment for `<first>`" message and exit code 0, but the remaining tools are not uninstalled.

Code snippet I tried to reproduce it.
```
aditya@aditya:/tmp/uv-tool-bug$ uv tool install ruff
Resolved 1 package in 750ms
Installed 1 package in 17ms
 + ruff==0.15.12
Installed 1 executable: ruff
warning: `/tmp/uv-tool-bug/bin` is not on your PATH. To use installed tools, run `export PATH="/tmp/uv-tool-bug/bin:$PATH"` or `uv tool update-shell`.
aditya@aditya:/tmp/uv-tool-bug$ uv tool install black
Resolved 7 packages in 688ms
Installed 7 packages in 16ms
 + black==26.3.1
 + click==8.3.3
 + mypy-extensions==1.1.0
 + packaging==26.2
 + pathspec==1.1.1
 + platformdirs==4.9.6
 + pytokens==0.4.1
Installed 2 executables: black, blackd
warning: `/tmp/uv-tool-bug/bin` is not on your PATH. To use installed tools, run `export PATH="/tmp/uv-tool-bug/bin:$PATH"` or `uv tool update-shell`.
aditya@aditya:/tmp/uv-tool-bug$ uv tool list
black v26.3.1
- black
- blackd
ruff v0.15.12
- ruff
aditya@aditya:/tmp/uv-tool-bug$ rm tools/ruff/uv-receipt.toml
aditya@aditya:/tmp/uv-tool-bug$ uv tool uninstall ruff black
Removed dangling environment for `ruff`
aditya@aditya:/tmp/uv-tool-bug$ uv tool list
black v26.3.1
- black
- blackd
```

If it's valid, let me know I will be happy to open a pr. 

### Platform

Ubuntu 24.04.2 LTS x86_64

### Version

uv 0.11.8 (502d42bf1 2026-04-28)

### Python version

result.title: `exclude-newer-package` silently ignored by `uv pip compile` when combined with global `exclude-newer`
result.body:
### Summary

First of all, thank you for contributing this amazing tool to the community. 

The [documentation](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/reference/settings/#exclude-newer-package) mentions that a global `exclude-newer` setting can be overwritten by using package specific `exclude-newer-package` settings. 

> Set a package to false to exempt it from the global [exclude-newer](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/reference/settings/#exclude-newer) constraint entirely.

This does not seem to work with `uv pip compile`

```sh
# create minimal requirements file with frequently updated package
printf "boto3" > req.in

# create config file 1 - global exclude-newer
printf 'exclude-newer = "7 days"\n' > config1.toml

# create config file 2 - global exclude-newer and then per-package overwrite
printf 'exclude-newer = "7 days"\nexclude-newer-package = { "boto3" = false }\n' > config2.toml

# compile environment
uv pip compile req.in 
# boto3==1.43.2

uv pip compile req.in --config-file config1.toml
# boto3==1.42.96

uv pip compile req.in --config-file config2.toml
# would have expected boto3==1.43.2, found boto3==1.42.96
```

I am not sure if I am misunderstanding how `--exclude-newer-package` works or in which context it works, but I expected the package level overwrite to work in the `config2.toml` examples

---

This behavior is consistent when using the CLI flags instead of a config file - although it seems the `uv pip compile` documentation does not explicitly mention the per-package-reset of global `exclude-newer` AFAICT. 

```sh
echo "boto3" > req.in

uv pip compile req.in --no-config -U
uv pip compile req.in --no-config -U  --exclude-newer "7 days"
uv pip compile req.in --no-config -U  --exclude-newer "7 days" --exclude-newer-package "boto3=false"
```

### Platform

Darwin 25.3.0 arm64

### Version

uv 0.11.8 (0e961dd9a 2026-04-27 aarch64-apple-darwin)

### Python version

Python 3.12.11

result.title: `[tool.uv.build-backend.data]` files are not installed in editable mode
result.body:
### Summary

Files declared in `[tool.uv.build-backend.data]` are correctly packaged into the wheel by `uv build`, and a non-editable `uv pip install <wheel>` correctly copies them to the right destination (e.g., the `purelib` slot lands at site-packages root, `scripts` at the venv's `bin/`).

But an editable install (`uv pip install -e .`) silently skips them: no data files land, no warning. The dropped files are gone in editable mode whether they're `.pth` files, binaries, configs, etc.

```toml
# pyproject.toml
[build-system]
build-backend = "uv_build"
requires = ["uv_build>=0.11,<0.12"]

[project]
name = "mypkg"
version = "0.1.0"
requires-python = ">=3.12"

[tool.uv.build-backend.data]
purelib = "data"
```

Layout:

```tree
uv-bug/
├── pyproject.toml
├── data/
│   └── mypkg-startup.pth
└── src/
    └── mypkg/
        └── __init__.py
```

Commands

```bash
mkdir uv-bug && cd uv-bug && uv venv
mkdir -p src/mypkg data && touch src/mypkg/__init__.py
echo 'import sys; print("[pth] fired", file=sys.stderr)' > data/mypkg-startup.pth
# Save the `pyproject.toml` block shown above as `uv-bug/pyproject.toml`.
export VIRTUAL_ENV="$PWD/.venv"  # so `uv pip install` targets this venv

# editable install: silent
# .pth never lands at site-packages root, doesn't fire
uv pip install -e .
.venv/bin/python -c ''

# non-editable install: .pth lands at site-packages root, fires on every startup
uv build --wheel
uv pip install --force-reinstall dist/*.whl
.venv/bin/python -c ''   # → "[pth] fired"
```

`<name>-<version>.data/` is the canonical way to ship arbitrary files alongside a Python package. With editable installs silently dropping them, development of any such project has a gap from production behavior in and editable dev setup.

### Additional context

[PEP 660](https://peps.python.org/pep-0660/) states that editable installs should match the regular-install behavior:

> When a project is installed in editable mode, users expect the installation to behave identically as a regular installation.

So `uv pip install -e .` silently dropping a `[tool.uv.build-backend.data]` can also be considered a divergence there.

For reference, Hatchling does not have this issue, one can use `tool.hatch.build.targets.wheel.force-include`.

```toml
# pyproject.toml
[build-system]
build-backend = "hatchling.build"
requires = ["hatchling"]

[project]
name = "mypkg"
version = "0.1.0"
requires-python = ">=3.12"

[tool.hatch.build.targets.wheel]
packages = ["src/mypkg"]

[tool.hatch.build.targets.wheel.force-include]
"data/mypkg-startup.pth" = "mypkg-startup.pth"
```

`uv pip install -e .` against this `pyproject.toml` lands `mypkg-startup.pth` at site-packages root, and a fresh `.venv/bin/python -c ''` fires it, matching my desired behavior.

I think it's worth extending `uv_build`'s editable hook to ship `[tool.uv.build-backend.data]` entries the same way hatchling's `force-include` does. Or at least emitting a warning when a data file is silently skipped in editable mode.

### Platform

Darwin 25.3.0 arm64

### Version

uv 0.11.8 (Homebrew 2026-04-27 aarch64-apple-darwin)

### Python version

Python 3.12.8

Thanks for the report! The `exclude-newer` hint is the part that matters here: aiobotocore 3.6.0 was published after your cutoff, so it was filtered out and the resolver fell back to 3.5.0.

### Summary

In my pyproject.toml, I have `aiobotocore~=3.6` as a dependency and `exclude-newer` set to 1 week.

aiobotocore 3.6.0 was released less than 1 week ago. This is uv's output:

```
  × No solution found when resolving dependencies:
  ╰─▶ Because only aiobotocore<=3.5.0 is available and your project depends on aiobotocore>=3.6,<4.dev0, we can conclude that your project's requirements are unsatisfiable.

      hint: `aiobotocore` was requested with a pre-release marker (e.g., aiobotocore>=3.6,<4.dev0), but pre-releases weren't enabled (try: `--prerelease=allow`)

      hint: `aiobotocore` was filtered by `exclude-newer` to only include packages uploaded before 2026-04-27T23:32:22.438447Z. The latest version satisfying the requirement is v3.6.0, published at
      2026-05-01T20:33:29.213Z. Consider using `exclude-newer-package` to override the cutoff for this package.
```

I don't really understand why it hints about pre-releases, but it's a bit misleading in this situation.

macOS 15 x86_64

result.title: Unable to use system-installed PyGObject (GTK) in uv venv, causing matplotlib to fall back to non-interactive backend
result.body:
### Summary

When using a virtual environment created by `uv venv` (without `--system-site-packages`), Python cannot import the `gi` module even though the necessary system package (`python-gobject`) is fully installed via the system package manager (Arch Linux, `pacman`). This causes matplotlib to fall back to the non-interactive `Agg` backend, preventing any plot windows from appearing.

The core issue is that standard virtual environments isolate from system site‑packages. While this is correct for pure Python packages, it breaks commonly used GUI libraries (GTK, Qt, Tk) that are often installed at the system level.

Current workarounds (`--system-site-packages`, manually compiling `PyGObject` in every project, `.pth` files) are fragile, non‑portable, or destroy environment isolation. A native `uv` mechanism to handle system‑level GUI dependencies would greatly improve the user experience for the many developers and scientists who rely on interactive plotting on Linux.

Desired solutions could include:
- A way to automatically detect and expose system packages required for common GUI backends.
- A built‑in hook or plugin system (similar to `virtualenvwrapper`'s `postmkvirtualenv`) allowing users to run custom steps after venv creation.
- A command‑line flag to include specific system packages (more granular than `--system-site-packages`).
- Official documentation or a recipe that solves the “matplotlib + GTK/Qt on Linux” problem once and for all.

### Example

## Current behavior (broken)

$ pacman -Q python-gobject
python-gobject 3.56.2-1

$ uv venv
$ source .venv/bin/activate
$ uv pip install matplotlib

$ python -c "import gi"
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "<string>", line 1, in <module>
ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'gi'

$ python -c "import matplotlib; print(matplotlib.get_backend())"
agg

## Desired behavior

After a hypothetical `uv` command like `uv venv --with-system-gui` (or an equivalent hook), the same setup would work out of the box:

$ uv venv --with-system-gui   # or similar mechanism
$ source .venv/bin/activate
$ uv pip install matplotlib

$ python -c "import gi; print('gi loaded successfully')"
gi loaded successfully

$ python -c "import matplotlib; print(matplotlib.get_backend())"
GTK3Agg   # or any interactive backend

This would allow interactive matplotlib plots to appear immediately, without additional manual steps.

- `uv venv --system-site-packages` makes system-installed packages visible in the venv. Note there are open issues about how this flag behaves in some cases (e.g. #4466, #17840), so it's worth checking that it works for your setup.
- Another option is to install PyGObject into the venv itself, which requires the system GObject/GTK development headers.

Your feature suggestions (a flag that exposes specific system packages, or a hook for post-venv setup) are useful, and we've noted them as a feature request. We can't commit to a timeline, but thanks for taking the time to describe the use case.

result.title: Regression in 0.11.9: `Failed to deserialize cache entry: invalid ID` for IDs written by older uv versions
result.body:
> ⚠️ **Note:** This issue was investigated and drafted with AI assistance (GitHub Copilot). The reproducer below has been executed and the failure was confirmed locally.

### Summary

Since 0.11.9 (PR #19201, "Remove our dependency on nanoid"), uv fails with `invalid ID: "<id>" (must be 16 ID characters in the alphabet)` when it encounters cache entries that were written by an older uv version. Older uv used `nanoid` with a 21-character token; the new `uv-fastid` deserializer strictly requires exactly 16 characters, so any pre-existing 21-character ID on disk now causes a hard failure instead of a cache miss.

The cache bucket version was intentionally not bumped in #19201, so existing caches on shared/CI workers are effectively poisoned after upgrading to 0.11.9 / 0.11.10.

### Reproduction

Self-contained shell reproducer (only requires `python3` + network for pip):

```bash
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Reproducer for uv 0.11.9/0.11.10 regression:
#   "Failed to deserialize cache entry: invalid ID ... (must be 16 ID characters in the alphabet)"
set -euo pipefail

WORK="$(mktemp -d)"
echo "Workdir: $WORK"
cd "$WORK"

export UV_CACHE_DIR="$WORK/uv-cache"
mkdir -p "$UV_CACHE_DIR"

mkdir -p pkg/src/dummy_pkg
cat > pkg/pyproject.toml <<'EOF'
[build-system]
requires = ["setuptools>=42"]
build-backend = "setuptools.build_meta"

[project]
name = "dummy-pkg"
version = "0.0.1"
EOF
: > pkg/src/dummy_pkg/__init__.py

python3 -m venv pkgbuild-venv
./pkgbuild-venv/bin/pip install -q build
./pkgbuild-venv/bin/python -m build --sdist --outdir dist pkg >/dev/null
SDIST="$(ls "$WORK"/dist/*.tar.gz)"

install_uv() {
    python3 -m venv "$2"
    "$2/bin/pip" install -q "uv==$1"
}

echo "=== Step 1: prime cache with uv 0.11.8 ==="
install_uv 0.11.8 "$WORK/uv-old"
python3 -m venv "$WORK/target-venv"
"$WORK/uv-old/bin/uv" pip install \
    --python "$WORK/target-venv/bin/python" \
    --reinstall --no-deps "$SDIST"

echo "=== Step 2: inspect IDs in the cache ==="
find "$UV_CACHE_DIR" -maxdepth 4 -type d -name 'archive-*' -print -exec sh -c '
    ls "$1" | head -n 5 | while read -r name; do
        printf "  %s (len=%d)\n" "$name" "${#name}"
    done
' _ {} \;

echo "=== Step 3: rerun with uv 0.11.10 against the SAME cache ==="
install_uv 0.11.10 "$WORK/uv-new"
"$WORK/uv-new/bin/uv" pip install \
    --python "$WORK/target-venv/bin/python" \
    --reinstall --no-deps "$SDIST"
```

### Observed output

```
=== Step 2: inspect IDs in the cache ===
/tmp/tmp.SA4yr9SC6n/uv-cache/archive-v0
  SzRiWVFFInsNaf0g33NFd (len=21)
  UKJkCZ3IOEXWTD5T0Le59 (len=21)

=== Step 3: rerun with uv 0.11.10 against the SAME cache ===
uv 0.11.10 (x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu)
Using Python 3.14.4 environment at: target-venv
  × Failed to build `dummy-pkg @
  │ file:///tmp/tmp.SA4yr9SC6n/dist/dummy_pkg-0.0.1.tar.gz`
  ├─▶ Failed to deserialize cache entry
  ╰─▶ invalid ID: "HM0NxJml5hc7UjbfTWT1r" (must be 16 ID characters in the
      alphabet)
```

The failing ID is exactly 21 characters — the old `nanoid` length. Note also that during the priming step uv 0.11.10 already prints `WARNING: Cache entry deserialization failed, entry ignored` for some entries, suggesting there is already a graceful-degrade path elsewhere in the codebase that the failing call site does not use.

### Expected behavior

Unrecognized/legacy ID formats should be treated as a cache miss (or be ignored / migrated), not aborted with a hard error — consistent with the discussion on #19201 where bumping the bucket was considered acceptable specifically to avoid this class of failure.

### Original CI failure (real-world trigger)

```
× Failed to build `voraus-release-test @ file:///.../voraus_release_test-2.25.1.dev8+g5bd0c2738.tar.gz`
├─▶ Failed to deserialize cache entry
╰─▶ invalid ID: "gtl3Kss14gljY4ur63X_i" (must be 16 ID characters in the alphabet)
```

Triggered via `tox-uv ~=1.29.0` (which pulls `uv<1,>=0.9.1`) on a long-lived Jenkins agent whose cache was previously populated by uv ≤ 0.11.8.

### Platform

result.title: `--dev` does not override `UV_NO_DEV=1`
result.body:
### Summary

[The uv docs say that](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/concepts/configuration-files/):

> Settings provided via environment variables take precedence over persistent configuration, and settings provided via the command line take precedence over both.

However, you can easily test that `uv run --dev` does not override `UV_NO_DEV=1`. I've created a repo that demonstrates this here: https://github.com/multimeric/UvNoDevBug. [In the workflow run](https://github.com/multimeric/UvNoDevBug/actions/runs/25469562411/job/74730301616), `pytest` is not available, which indicates that `UV_NO_DEV=1` is winning.

### Platform

Tested on MacOS 15.6 and Ubuntu 24.04.4

### Version

0.11.10, 0.11.11

### Python version

3.12

result.title: Installation fails if a direct dependency pins a prerelease package
result.body:
### Summary

Installing a non-prerelease package that pins a prerelease package fails. It suggests to use `--prerelease=allow`, but this is bad UX IMO, as there is only one correct way to do things here. Arguably worse, it means people will silently not get the latest version when installing.

We just released `max==26.3.0` which depends on `mojo-compiler==1.0.0b1`. Trying to install `max==26.3.0` gives this:

```sh
~/Documents/modular/scratch$ uv pip install max==26.3.0
  × No solution found when resolving dependencies:
  ╰─▶ Because there is no version of mojo-compiler==1.0.0b1 and max-core==26.3.0 depends on mojo-compiler==1.0.0b1, we can conclude that max-core==26.3.0 cannot be used.
      And because max==26.3.0 depends on max-core==26.3.0 and you require max==26.3.0, we can conclude that your requirements are unsatisfiable.

      hint: `mojo-compiler` was requested with a pre-release marker (e.g., mojo-compiler==1.0.0b1), but pre-releases weren't enabled (try: `--prerelease=allow`)
```

My understanding is that the resolver completely ignores prelease packages unless one of two things happens:
1. The package is specifically requested
2. `--prerelease=allow` is set.

However in this case, there is no way to install `max==26.3.0` without prerelease packages. I believe in this case (at least) we shouldn't need `--prerelease=allow`. I've also seen another case like this:
```sh
~/Documents/modular/scratch$ uv pip install sglang==0.5.10
  × No solution found when resolving dependencies:
  ╰─▶ Because only flash-attn-4<4.0.0b4 is available and sglang==0.5.10 depends on flash-attn-4>=4.0.0b4, we can conclude that sglang==0.5.10 cannot be used.
      And because you require sglang==0.5.10, we can conclude that your requirements are unsatisfiable.

      hint: `flash-attn-4` was requested with a pre-release marker (e.g., flash-attn-4>=4.0.0b4), but pre-releases weren't enabled (try: `--prerelease=allow`)
```

Perhaps if the requirements are unsatisfiable without prereleases, we could allow them (or at least the bare minimum necessary to resolve).

Admittedly, I think the `--prerelease=allow` flag has caused more headaches for me than problems it's solved, though I am working with largely pre-release packages so there's a bias there. If it were up to me I would flip the default, though I understand the intentions behind it.

### Platform

Linux 6.18.7-76061807-generic x86_64 GNU/Linux

### Version

uv 0.11.11 (x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu)

### Python version

Python 3.14

result.title: `uv tree` displaying not installed extras
result.body:
### Summary

When running `uv tree` (or `uv tree --no-dedupe`) the dependencies are not differentiated based on their extras.

## Example

### `pyproject.toml`
```
[project]
name = "test"
version = "0.1.0"
requires-python = ">=3.12"
dependencies = ["asyncssh"]

[dependency-groups]
dev = ["asyncssh[bcrypt]"]
```
### Output: 
```
test v0.1.0
├── asyncssh v2.21.1
│   ├── cryptography v46.0.5
│   │   └── cffi v2.0.0
│   │       └── pycparser v2.23
│   ├── typing-extensions v4.15.0
│   └── bcrypt v5.0.0 (extra: bcrypt)
└── asyncssh[bcrypt] v2.21.1 (group: dev)
    ├── cryptography v46.0.5
    │   └── cffi v2.0.0
    │       └── pycparser v2.23
    ├── typing-extensions v4.15.0
    └── bcrypt v5.0.0 (extra: bcrypt)
```
### Expected Output: 
```
test v0.1.0
├── asyncssh v2.21.1
│   ├── cryptography v46.0.5
│   │   └── cffi v2.0.0
│   │       └── pycparser v2.23
│   └── typing-extensions v4.15.0
└── asyncssh[bcrypt] v2.21.1 (group: dev)
    ├── cryptography v46.0.5
    │   └── cffi v2.0.0
    │       └── pycparser v2.23
    ├── typing-extensions v4.15.0
    └── bcrypt v5.0.0 (extra: bcrypt)
```

This also happens in workplaces where only one package defines an extra.

### Platform

Windows, Linux

### Version

uv 0.11.11

### Python version

3.12

Triage for astral-sh/uv#19327: "`uv tree` displaying not installed extras"

**Summary:** `uv tree` shows extras as if they were installed when they aren't. In the example, `bcrypt` appears under the default `asyncssh` entry with `(extra: bcrypt)`, even though only the `dev` group requests `asyncssh[bcrypt]`. **Suggested labels:**
- `bug`: the output is incorrect compared to the expected output in the report.
- `area:cli`: the problem is in the command's displayed output. This is a judgment call; `area:projects` or `area:lock` could also fit if maintainers see it as a resolution issue.

**Duplicate check:** Two searches turned up no earlier issue reporting this problem. The closest hits (#12290, #13785, #9734, #6907) are about PyTorch, `uv sync`, and resolution failures, so I did not mark this as a duplicate.

**Reproduction:** The report includes a complete `pyproject.toml`, the actual output, and the expected output. It does not need `needs-mre`.

**Draft reply:** Drafted but not posted. It thanks the reporter, confirms the behavior described (the extra shown under the default `asyncssh` entry without being requested), and says the issue is labeled as a bug for maintainers. It makes no promises about a fix or timeline.

**Final triage:** Label as `bug` (and `area:cli` if you agree), leave it open, no duplicate link, and post the drafted reply after review.

**Environment:**

- uv version: 0.11.12 (63c5f57d3 2026-05-08 x86_64-pc-windows-msvc)
- System Python: CPython 3.12.6 (C:\Python312\python.exe)  works fine

When creating a venv with `uv venv .venv` and running any Python script 
that imports openai/httpx, I get:

OPENSSL_Uplink(00007FF93EAF9C60,08): no OPENSSL_Applink

2. .venv\Scripts\Activate.ps1
3. uv pip install openai
4. python -c "import openai"
-> OPENSSL_Uplink error

**Was working fine previously, broke recently without any changes on my end.**

### Platform

Windows 11

### Version

uv version: 0.11.12 (63c5f57d3 2026-05-08 x86_64-pc-windows-msvc)

Python 3.12.6

result.title: `uv pip compile` ignores `required-environments`
result.body:
### Summary

`uv pip compile` seems to ignore `required-environments`, which differs in behavior from `uv lock`

Let's use `hdbscan` as our test subject. It does not publish Linux ARM wheels for Python 3.12. If we have this  `pyproject.toml`, where we add Python 3.12 Linux ARM to `required-environments` and use `no-build = true`:

```pyproject.toml
[project]
name = "test"
version = "0.0.1"
requires-python = ">=3.12"
dependencies = ["hdbscan==0.8.42"]

[tool.uv]
no-build = true
required-environments = [
  "python_version == '3.12' and sys_platform == 'linux' and platform_machine == 'aarch64'",
]
```

We can see that:
- `uv pip compile` + `required-environments` runs without an error (unexpected)
  ```shell
  > uv pip compile --generate-hashes --no-annotate --no-header --no-deps --universal
  
  hdbscan==0.8.42 \
      --hash=sha256:1459d777d16800361b504656982ae3988fc412b97a8f244ffbd565c72a39ca41 \
      --hash=sha256:2ab4c7fba52f648fe4276d7b60f6831a9009089872a5ca05f91d6ed1bbe52d23 \
      --hash=sha256:2c86d215b5940a5414ceb468af5987941d3526e49d09418296830528161ccdd6 \
      --hash=sha256:31541afa4ce2d42ad828ffd5da1bf40d8212fa8318cc28e58c65ffe719e9083b \
      --hash=sha256:3bd749a3df39c7e965bd8b2173c3804cdb11ad73d524a5df1201360814293614 \
      --hash=sha256:7e0f160ee0d5e61d9a2411c44fa41c12849e814899851cab8e17e924487018e1 \
      --hash=sha256:990b9f9ce14f290eb8bd9343048cb50b890560de99ced4fb31c486cb0c9f0f74 \
      --hash=sha256:bc428bff42b9ec8ecbaf5d790b6b6de9e2cb120059350d0caecb92311f44b869 \
      --hash=sha256:cd86e30bfe1f1363b9b97a8a84cbeebf761c5ff4262037f9cf0d068b590fe541 \
      --hash=sha256:e14d7309c91e1a59f592936555fe4282e66061719225d9cb2d7bf18040bb8b54 \
      --hash=sha256:f0cc0f279f0f83203277fb5b09422cbfab577fe269e3f71d0082354f65d71cf3 \
      --hash=sha256:f265f1ae267713c7a8dfa14ddc530c1ccf87905cf003db65769b9afed519d910 \
      --hash=sha256:fd9f0d5f65a5aa4437b8f69ff8cb4ae6d42723e543254dca49c62f02192c2791
  ```
- `uv lock` + `required-environments` errors (expected)
  ```shell
  > uv lock
  Using CPython 3.12.13
    × No solution found when resolving dependencies for split (markers: python_full_version == '3.12.*' and platform_machine == 'aarch64' and sys_platform == 'linux'):
    ╰─▶ Because hdbscan==0.8.42 has no `python_full_version == '3.12.*' and platform_machine == 'aarch64' and sys_platform == 'linux'`-compatible wheels and your project depends on
        hdbscan==0.8.42, we can conclude that your project's requirements are unsatisfiable.
  
        hint: The resolution failed for an environment that is not the current one, consider limiting the environments with `tool.uv.environments`.
  ```

If we instead use `environments`
```pyproject.toml
[project]
name = "test"
version = "0.0.1"
requires-python = ">=3.12"
dependencies = ["hdbscan==0.8.42"]

[tool.uv]
no-build = true
environments = [
  "python_version == '3.12' and sys_platform == 'linux' and platform_machine == 'aarch64'",
]
```

- `uv pip compile` + `environments` _does_ error
  ```shell
  > uv pip compile --generate-hashes --no-annotate --no-header --no-deps --universal
  × No solution found when resolving dependencies for split (markers: python_full_version == '3.12.*' and platform_machine == 'aarch64' and sys_platform == 'linux'):
    ╰─▶ Because hdbscan==0.8.42 has no `python_full_version == '3.12.*' and platform_machine == 'aarch64' and sys_platform == 'linux'`-compatible wheels and you require hdbscan==0.8.42, we
        can conclude that your requirements are unsatisfiable.
  
        hint: The resolution failed for an environment that is not the current one, consider limiting the environments with `tool.uv.environments`.
  ```

This seems backwards to me, based on the docs:

https://docs.astral.sh/uv/reference/settings/#required-environments

> By default, uv requires each package to include at least one wheel that is compatible with the designated Python version. The `required-environments` setting can be used to ensure that the resulting re

## Triage: astral-sh/uv#19372, "`uv pip compile` ignores `required-environments`"

**Summary:** With `required-environments` set for Linux aarch64 / Python 3.12, `uv lock` correctly fails because `hdbscan==0.8.42` has no compatible wheel. `uv pip compile --universal` with the same config succeeds silently. The docs say `required-environments` should guarantee a compatible wheel for each required environment, so the pip interface appears to be the one that's wrong.

**Suggested labels:**
- `bug`: the documented behavior isn't honored by `uv pip compile`.
- `area:uv-pip`: the affected interface is the `uv pip` subcommand.
- `area:resolver`: the problem is in how required environments are enforced during resolution.

I did not apply these. I only have tools to read labels and draft comments, so a maintainer will need to add them.

**Duplicates:** No duplicate found. The closest matches were related but different:
- #17068 (index strategies ignored with `[required-]environments`)
- #12782 (`fork-strategy fewest` with `required-environments`)
- #17382 (documents a marker limitation in `required-environments`)

I didn't mark it as a duplicate. The related issues are about other settings, not the `uv pip compile` vs. `uv lock` mismatch. A maintainer may still want to check #17382 in case the marker limitation explains part of this.

**Draft reply:** Drafted, not posted. It thanks the reporter for the reproduction and says the mismatch looks worth investigating. It makes no promises about fixes or timelines.

**Final triage:** Bug in `uv pip compile`. Labels `bug`, `area:uv-pip`, and `area:resolver` are suggested. No duplicate. Needs a maintainer to review and apply labels and post the reply.

result.title: uv-build includes empty directories in bdist/sdist
result.body:
### Summary

We are considering switching from setuptools to uv-build as our build backend, and I'm trying to first achieve bit-for-bit reproducibility. One thing I noticed is that uv-build appears to include empty directories in the bdist/sdist whereas setuptools does not. These empty directories can be the result of switching back-and-forth between git branches or renaming directories where only a `__pycache__` directory remains in the old directory.

Steps to reproduce:

1. Clone any project using uv-build as the build backend
2. Add an empty directory, possibly with a `__pycache__` sub-directory
3. Run `uv build`
4. Run `tar tf dist/*.tar.gz` and/or `unzip -l dist/*.whl` to inspect which files are included

You should find that your empty directory is present in the sdist/bdist.

### Platform

macOS 26.4.1 arm64

### Version

uv 0.11.6 (aarch64-apple-darwin)

### Python version

Python 3.13.7

result.title: Git credentials in workspace member `[tool.uv.sources]` not applied under `uv sync --frozen`
result.body:
### Summary

When `uv sync --frozen` is run against a workspace, credentials embedded in
`[tool.uv.sources]` entries that live in **workspace-member** `pyproject.toml`
files are silently dropped. The same entries work correctly under `uv lock`
and `uv sync` (without `--frozen`). For private git deps this manifests as
`fatal: could not read Username for 'https://github.com': terminal prompts disabled`.

### Minimal reproducible example

```
repo/
├── pyproject.toml              # workspace root; declares members; no [tool.uv.sources]
├── uv.lock
└── nested/
    └── pyproject.toml          # [tool.uv.sources]
                                # example = { git = "https://user:<EMAIL_1>/organization/repository", tag = "v1" }
```

Root `pyproject.toml`:

```toml
[project]
name = "root"
version = "0"
requires-python = ">=3.12"
dependencies = ["example"]

[tool.uv.workspace]
members = ["nested"]
```

`nested/pyproject.toml`:

```toml
[project]
name = "nested"
version = "0"
requires-python = ">=3.12"
dependencies = ["example"]

[tool.uv.sources]
example = { git = "https://user:<EMAIL_1>/organization/repository", tag = "v1" }
```

Steps:

1. `uv lock` from the repo root — succeeds; lockfile correctly records
   `git+https://github.com/organization/repository@<commit>` with no credentials (per
   the redaction behavior introduced in #5803).
2. `uv sync --frozen` from the repo root — **fails**:

   ```
   × Failed to download and build `example @ git+https://github.com/organization/repository@<commit>`
   ├─▶ Git operation failed
   ├─▶ failed to clone into: /root/.cache/uv/git-v0/db/...
   ├─▶ failed to fetch commit `<commit>`
   ╰─▶ process didn't exit successfully:
       `/usr/bin/git fetch --force --update-head-ok 'https://github.com/organization/repository' ...`
       (exit status: 128)
       --- stderr
       fatal: could not read Username for 'https://github.com': terminal prompts disabled
   ```

Workaround: move the credentialed `[tool.uv.sources]` entry into the
workspace-root `pyproject.toml`, or configure git directly via
`git config --global url.<auth>.insteadOf <bare>` / `GIT_ASKPASS` / `.netrc`.

### Root cause

Under `--frozen`, project discovery is intentionally scoped to the root only:

https://github.com/astral-sh/uv/blob/a4d9e42197d606474f085cff93caa200666512df/crates/uv/src/commands/project/sync.rs#L101-L110

`store_credentials_from_target` then iterates `target.sources()`, which walks
`workspace.sources()` plus each loaded member's `[tool.uv.sources]`:

https://github.com/astral-sh/uv/blob/a4d9e42197d606474f085cff93caa200666512df/crates/uv/src/commands/project/install_target.rs#L150-L174

With `MemberDiscovery::None`, members aren't loaded, so member-level
`[tool.uv.sources]` are invisible to `store_credentials_from_target`, and
`GIT_STORE` never gets the credentials. `GitSource::fetch` then runs against
the bare URL:

https://github.com/astral-sh/uv/blob/a4d9e42197d606474f085cff93caa200666512df/crates/uv-git/src/source.rs#L69-L75

### Expected behavior

`uv sync --frozen` should respect credentials defined in any workspace
member's `[tool.uv.sources]`, consistently with `uv lock` and `uv sync`
without `--frozen`. The lockfile already records workspace membership, so
credentials can be collected from each member's `pyproject.toml` on disk
without doing full member discovery / validation.

### Related

- #5803 — Redact registry credentials in lockfile (established that creds in
  `pyproject.toml` must be re-applied at install time; this issue is a
  follow-up where re-application is incomplete for workspaces under
  `--frozen`).
- #8529 — Provide a way to provide Git authentication for `tool.uv.sources`
  (broader umbrella; this issue is the concrete `--frozen` subset).

### Platform

macOS 26 arm64

### Version

uv 0.11.14 (3fdfdc7d4 2026-05-12 aarch64-apple-darwin)

### Python version

Python 3.14.2

result.title: Does `uv tool install` read `[[tool.uv]]` section of target `pyproject.toml`
result.body:
### Question

I have a package with dependencies from a private index which is defined in the `[[tool.uv]]` section of the `pyproject.toml`:

```toml
dependencies = [
    "my-dependency", 
]

[tool.uv]
keyring-provider = "subprocess"

[tool.uv.sources]
my-dependency = { index = "my-index" }

[[tool.uv.index]]
name = "my-index"
url = "...."
explicit = true
```

When installing that package from a local path with `uv tool install .` or from the github repo `uv tool install "my-package @ git+ssh://<EMAIL_1>/xyz"` the `my-dependency` package is installed without issues. I didn't expect this to work because I didn't pass the private index with `--index` to the tool command. 

The [Configuration files](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/concepts/configuration-files/) docs say *"For `tool` commands... local configuration files will be ignored"* which matches @zanieb's comment [here](https://github.com/astral-sh/uv/issues/16021#issuecomment-3334132268). Therefore, I would have expected the `[[tool.uv]]` section of the `pyproject.toml` to be ignored in which case the `my-dependency` package should not have been found.

If I try to install `my-package` with `pip install "my-package @ git+ssh://<EMAIL_1>/xyz"` I get the expected error that no package `my-dependency` was found.

Can anyone explain this behavior?



### Platform

Ubuntu 24.04 x86_64

### Version

uv 0.11.15

result.title: python builds are missing AF_VSOCK
result.body:
### Summary

the address family AF_VSOCK was added in linux 3.9 and python 3.7, respectively, but seems to be missing from your python builds.

As such, anything using `socket.AF_VSOCK` fails - namely https://github.com/systemd/mkosi , and probably also the libvirt python bindings.

### Platform

Linux 5.14.0-611.55.1.el9_7.x86_64 x86_64 GNU/Linux

### Version

uv 0.11.15 (x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu)

### Python version

Python 3.14.5

**Summary:** The reporter says the Python builds that uv installs don't define `socket.AF_VSOCK`, so tools that use it fail. Examples are systemd's mkosi and probably the libvirt Python bindings. The reporter is on uv 0.11.15 with Python 3.14.5 on RHEL 9 (kernel 5.14).

**Suggested labels** (all confirmed to exist in the repo):
- `bug`: a standard library constant that should be present is missing.
- `area:cpython`: the problem is with the CPython build itself.
- `area:uv-python`: the issue concerns the Python installation interface.
- `external`: the likely cause is python-build-standalone, which uv downloads, so the root cause is outside uv. This is my inference from the report and I haven't verified it.

It thanks the reporter, explains that the builds come from python-build-standalone, says the team will look into where the constant goes missing, and asks for the uv version and a quick `hasattr(socket, 'AF_VSOCK')` check. It makes no promises about fixes or timelines.

**Next steps for maintainers:**
- Confirm whether python-build-standalone's Linux builds are compiled without `AF_VSOCK` support, for example because the build uses older kernel headers. If so, the fix belongs upstream, and an issue should be filed there and linked here.
- Decide whether to keep `external` or drop it once that's confirmed.

Thanks for the report, and for narrowing it down to 0.11.15 with a clean rollback to 0.11.14.

### Summary

After updating to the latest version of uv `0.11.15` I noticed the following error in our docker build:
```
 > [builder 4/8] RUN --mount=type=cache,target=/root/.cache     uv sync --frozen --no-dev --no-install-local --no-install-project :
0.105 error: invalid value '' for '--no-binary-package <NO_BINARY_PACKAGE>': Not a valid package or extra name: "". Names must start and end with a letter or digit and may only contain -, _, ., and alphanumeric characters.
0.105 
0.105 For more information, try '--help'.
```

We have this in our dockerfile:
```
ARG UV_NO_BINARY_PACKAGE=""
ENV UV_NO_BINARY_PACKAGE=${UV_NO_BINARY_PACKAGE}
```

I assume it's related to this recent change: https://github.com/astral-sh/uv/pull/19435

I rolled back to `0.11.14` and confirmed it worked previously. I wonder if that validation should be on cli args only?

### Platform

Debian

0.11.15

3.11

**Triage for astral-sh/uv#19499: "Validation on empty environment variables"**

**Summary:** After upgrading to uv 0.11.15, a Docker build fails because `UV_NO_BINARY_PACKAGE` is set to an empty string. uv now rejects the empty value as an invalid package name. The reporter rolled back to 0.11.14 and confirmed the build worked. They suspect PR #19435 and suggest the validation should apply only to CLI arguments, not environment variables.

**Suggested labels:**
- `bug`: this is a regression where a previously working setup now fails.
- `area:cli`: the failure comes from argument/value validation for a CLI option.
- `area:configuration`: the problem involves an environment variable setting.

I left out `area:error-messages`. The error message is clear, but the real issue is the validation itself.

**Duplicates:** No duplicate found. Searches for empty environment variables and this error text returned no matching earlier issues, so I did not mark it as a duplicate.

It thanks the reporter for the bisect, explains that empty env vars are being rejected by the new validation, notes the CLI-only suggestion as useful input, and offers a workaround: don't set `UV_NO_BINARY_PACKAGE` when the build arg is empty. It makes no promises about a fix or timeline.

**Notes for maintainers:**
- The root cause is unverified. I haven't checked PR #19435, so the attribution rests on the reporter's suspicion.
- Before the fix, decide whether empty env vars should be treated as unset across all options or only for this one. That is probably the main design question.

result.title: Document malware check behavior
result.body:
The public docs should document https://github.com/astral-sh/uv/issues/18781 (particularly after we remove it from preview).

Some key things we should document:

* We use OSV for malware reports, and users can configure their own API-compatible OSV service if they're hosting one.
* OSV in turn uses https://github.com/ossf/malicious-packages for `MAL` advisories. `MAL` advisories are not propagated directly by PyPI, and are produced on timelines that aren't related directly to quarantine actions on PyPI.
* Malware checks are performed on locked resolutions, since installing from a lockfile doesn't re-access the index. For resolution itself, the equivalent behavior is controlled by PyPI's own quarantining abilities.

result.title: `uv tool install -e .` does not interact correctly with `dynamic` field of `pyproject.toml`
result.body:
### Summary

Sorry I don't know how to produce a minimum working example for this.

Running `uv tool install .` works as expected. However, running `uv tool install -e .` installs an older version of the package. This misses executables, which I have set up in the following way:

My `setup.py` fetches the scripts dynamically like so:

```python
# pyproject.toml
...
dynamic = ['scripts', 'version']
...
```

```python
# setup.py
...
setup(
    version=version,
    entry_points={
            'console_scripts': [
                    my_module_name + '-' + f'{filename_to_command_name(script_name):s}' + ' = ' + my_module_name + 
                        f'.scripts.{remove_extension_from_filename(script_name):s}:main'
                    for script_name in my_scripts
            ]
        },
)
```
It seems that `uv` is caching the package or something, since it adds all the executables except the most recently added one.

Running `uv tool install .` followed by `uv tool install -e .` shows that the version of the package is downgraded to one which is below the current version in the index... it must either be reading from a cache or from the git repository history.
```
Installed 1 package in 18ms
 - my-module-name==0.22.2.dev4 (from file:///home/user/my-module-name)
 + my-module-name==0.22.0 (from file:///home/user/my-module-name)
```

I've noticed that changing the contents of `setup.py` causes `uv` to invalidate whatever cache is being used, and resolves the issue. This is the second time I've observed this issue, so I guess that `uv` is making a false assumption that if `setup.py` is not changed, then the version and list of executables must also not be changed. This is not the case.

### Platform

Linux 7.0.3-arch1-2 x86_64 GNU/Linux

### Version

uv 0.11.11 (ed7b06001 2026-05-06 x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu)

### Python version

Python 3.12.12
